Title: Snakes, swings and stuck rings: Fire Dept's strangest rescues
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR:    Removing rings from sensitive body parts, freeing children wedged in cooking pots, carrying patients weighing 200kg down narrow staircases and rescuing adults stuck in playground equipment are all in a day's work for  firefighters.
While the Fire and Rescue Department is best known for fighting fires and responding to road accidents, it is increasingly called upon to handle unusual rescue operations that require precision, patience and compassion.
And these are no longer isolated or occasional calls.
Department director-general Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad said it handled 72,977 special rescue operations nationwide last year, a 10.1 per cent increase from 66,299 cases in 2024.
Firefighters recorded 31,965 such incidents between January and June last year — an average of 177 a day.
The increase reflects greater public awareness of emergency services, continued urban development and a wider range of incidents requiring specialised rescue expertise.
"It also reflects the expanding scope of the department's responsibilities, which now covers a wide range of incidents requiring specialised rescue expertise."
Among the most delicate operations, he said, were those involving the removal of metal rings and other objects from a man's genitalia.
"These cases require a high level of precision and composure. Firefighters use a specialised ring cutter while cooling the area with running water to prevent heat build-up and injury to sensitive tissue."
Another recurring rescue involves children who become trapped after getting their heads stuck in cooking pots, plastic chairs or metal grilles.
Nor Hisham said beyond the technical challenge of cutting through metal or plastic in confined spaces, firefighters also had to calm frightened children before carrying out the rescue.
"Children often panic, cry and struggle. Our personnel must first reassure and calm them before carefully using hydraulic rescue equipment in confined spaces."
But the department's special rescue workload extends far beyond such unusual cases.
Humanitarian assistance accounted for most special rescue tasks last year, with 57,957 cases, followed by 5,927 natural disasters, 4,667 building and structural emergencies, 3,448 hazardous materials spills and leaks, and 978 search-and-rescue operations.
Nor Hisham said firefighters were also regularly called upon to assist hospitals in transporting people with severe obesity, some weighing more than 200kg, from upper-floor flats without lifts.
"Such operations require careful coordination to ensure the safety of both the patient and rescuers as they manoeuvre reinforced stretchers through narrow staircases," he said.
Other unusual rescues include freeing victims whose hands become trapped inside toilet bowls or food-processing machines.
Firefighters would painstakingly dismantle porcelain fixtures or machine parts bit by bit to avoid causing further injury.
He added that in one memorable case in 2023, firefighters rescued an adult woman who became stuck in a children's swing at a playground.
Nor Hisham said while the technical rescue itself was relatively straightforward, firefighters also had to protect the woman's dignity as curious onlookers gathered and some attempted to record the incident on their mobile phones.
"Our personnel handled the situation professionally while protecting the victim's privacy and dignity," he said.
The growing workload has also required the department to maintain a wide range of specialised equipment, including hydraulic rescue tools, hazardous materials detection equipment, rescue boats, confined-space rescue systems, drones, specialised emergency vehicles and communications equipment.
Despite the rising number of special rescue operations, Nor Hisham stressed that the department's readiness to respond to fires and other major emergencies had not been affected.
He said it maintained its operational capability through strategic deployment of personnel and assets, continuous monitoring of readiness levels and prioritisation of incidents according to risk.
The department also recorded 156 false or non-actionable emergency calls involving special rescues between 2024 and June this year — comprising 63 cases in 2024, 78 last year and 15 in the first half of this year.
Nor Hisham urged the public to use the 999 emergency line responsibly and provide accurate details, including the exact location, nature of the emergency and condition of victims, to enable a swift response to genuine life-threatening situations.
Despite the unusual nature of many of the calls, Nor Hisham stressed that every rescue was treated with the same urgency and professionalism.
He said each incident presented its own challenges and often required firefighters to combine technical expertise with empathy, particularly when victims were distressed, embarrassed or in pain.

Title: Lala, now a hurricane, dumps heavy rain on Hawaii
Article:
HONOLULU: Hurricane Lala on Saturday lashed Hawaii's Big Island with heavy rain and strong winds, as forecasters warned of potentially dangerous flooding across the US Pacific island state.
Lala strengthened into a Category 1 hurricane at around 9am local time (1900 GMT), packing winds of up to 75 miles per hour (120 kilometres per hour).
A hurricane warning was in effect for Hawaii County, which covers the Big Island, and a tropical storm warning was in place for the state's seven other major islands: Maui, Molokai, Kahoolawe, Lanai, Oahu, Kauai and Niihau.
Lala was expected to dump 10 to 20 inches (25 to 50 cm) of rain on the Big Island, with totals possibly reaching 25 inches.
"This rainfall will produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas of steep terrain," the US National Hurricane Centre said in its 1800 GMT advisory.
A storm surge of one to three feet will be accompanied by "large and dangerous waves," it said. Swells generated by Lala would build through the weekend and are likely to cause "life-threatening surf and rip current conditions."
The rough conditions could persist into Sunday.
"It's a serious storm," Governor Josh Green said, proclaiming a state of emergency to ensure Hawaii and its counties "have sufficient resources to clear debris, secure infrastructure, and take other measures to prepare."
Honolulu Mayor Rick Blangiardi said Friday his administration had spent days preparing for the storm, and urged residents to be ready.
Drivers were seen filling up their vehicles with gasoline.
The state was last hit by a "major" hurricane – meaning Category 3, 4, or 5 on the Saffir-Simpson scale – in 1992, when Hurricane Iniki caused at least six deaths and billions of dollars in damage.
Hawaii was menaced by Hurricane Fausto last month, before the storm weakened and skirted north of the island chain.
EL NINO
The storm comes as a powerful El Nino has formed in the central equatorial Pacific Ocean.
Temperatures are already so high that the National Oceanic and Atmosphere Administration now predicts a 69 percent chance of a "historic event that would exceed the strength of previous El Nino events dating back to 1950" when it peaks between October and December.
El Nino, a natural climate pattern when sea surface temperatures in the central and eastern Pacific Ocean become unusually warm, tends to promote hurricane activity in the Pacific while suppressing it in the Atlantic.
Human-caused climate change can amplify El Nino's impacts because a warmer ocean and atmosphere increase the availability of energy and moisture for extreme weather events, such as heat waves and heavy rainfall.
Hawaii's emergency management agency recommended residents clear gutters and drains and move valuables off the ground, seal gaps in doors and remove tree limbs that threaten their properties.

Title: Iran fires back at Trump's threat to declare Hormuz a US territory
Article:
TEHERAN: Iran on Saturday fired back at US President Donald Trump's claim that he would soon declare the Strait of Hormuz part of US territory, saying the crucial energy waterway it has blockaded "will remain Iranian."
Trump has repeatedly insisted that the strait, which Tehran effectively closed at the start of the Middle East war in late February, is under US control despite traffic remaining throttled.
"The Strait of Hormuz has been Iranian, is Iranian, and will remain Iranian," Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi said on X.
"This strait will only be closed and opened under Iran's command."
Trump told a political rally in New York state on Friday that after the US defeats Iran, "pretty soon I'll be declaring the Hormuz Strait a territory of the United States."
"It's true," he added.
An unnamed White House official later clarified that Trump was joking, the Wall Street Journal reported.
Last week, a top Iranian official set out a list of conditions for reopening the strait, including an end to the "war and aggression against Iran and its allies in Lebanon, Palestine, Yemen, and Iraq."
Mohammad Bagher Zolghadr also demanded the end of crippling sanctions, the release of frozen assets and compensation for wartime damage.
ONGOING ATTACKS
As diplomacy stalls between the longtime foes, attacks in the Hormuz strait have continued, highlighting the continued risks to regional shipping.
The United Arab Emirates' state-owned oil giant ADNOC said on Saturday that one of its vessels came under attack the night before.
Abu Dhabi's foreign ministry later blamed Tehran, and said that Iran's Revolutionary Guards were engaged in "acts of piracy" in the strait.
On Friday the Gulf nation blamed Iran for other attacks on two vessels linked to ADNOC as they passed through the waterway.
Such attacks led to the collapse of an April ceasefire between the United States and Iran.
As Iran chokes traffic in Hormuz, its Houthi allies in Yemen have also declared a parallel maritime blockade on Saudi ports in the Red Sea, the oil-exporting giant's only other maritime route.
A June deal between Washington and Teheran – meant to serve as a jumping-off point for negotiations on a permanent settlement – had said Iran and Oman would hash out future arrangements for the Hormuz in discussion with other Gulf countries and "in line with the applicable international law."
Before the war, the strait carried around a fifth of the world's oil and LNG exports, and prices have repeatedly surged since the dispute over the waterway erupted, piling economic and political pressure on Washington.
Iran wants to control the strait and charge tolls, powers it did not exercise before the war and ones that the US fiercely opposes.
The closure of Hormuz has driven up prices for US voters, creating a political headache for Trump as November's midterm elections near.
US Vice President JD Vance said this week that Washington's top priority in the Iran war was keeping energy prices low for Americans, while preventing Teheran from acquiring a nuclear weapon ranked second.
Teheran signalled last week that it had agreed with Oman on a route for ships to transit the strait and were finalising arrangements to jointly manage the waterway.
The US has imposed its own retaliatory blockade of Iranian ports in an attempt to cripple its economy.
"We have the blockade. No ships get through unless we want them to," Trump said to a cheering crowd of supporters on Friday.

Title: Opposition walkouts may win headlines but lose the debate
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Opposition walkouts may deliver powerful visuals and generate headlines, but their effectiveness as a parliamentary weapon  depends on whether they turn   into meaningful political or institutional pressure.
The tactic has long been used by opposition parties  to protest  contentious legislation, parliamentary procedures and major national issues.
But walking out also means giving up  the floor when members of parliament can  question the government, challenge its position and put  objections on record.
The issue came into focus during the  Dewan Rakyat sitting on the Royal Commission of Inquiry report on Tabung Haji.
Several    opposition MPs walked out after their  bid to postpone the sitting  until  Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim could attend was rejected.
Opposition chief whip Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said  the Tabung Haji issue was significant enough to warrant the prime minister's presence, particularly as Anwar had previously addressed it.
The opposition also questioned the value of  a ministerial briefing in Anwar's absence.
When the sitting proceeded with Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi and other ministers present, several opposition MPs left the chamber.
WALKOUT'S LIMITED IMPACT
Universiti Malaya Department of Political Science, Public Administration and Development Studies senior lecturer Dr Mohammad Tawfik Yaakub said walkouts were a legitimate form of political protest, but had  limited impact  if parliamentary proceedings could continue.
"If the sitting continues, the government can still provide explanations and other MPs can continue debating, so the institutional impact becomes very limited," he said.
"In such circumstances, a walkout can  be seen as political theatre, producing pictures, headlines and social media content, but not necessarily changing decisions or increasing government accountability."
Tawfik said he understood the opposition's argument that the Tabung Haji issue  warranted Anwar's presence, but remaining in the chamber would have been a stronger  strategy.
"They could have recorded their objections in Hansard and remained in the House to challenge the report with facts, documents and arguments."
He said the decision by some opposition MPs to stay also showed a lack of consensus  over the walkout.
Bersatu MPs  argued that the Tabung Haji issue was too important to be turned into "political drama".
Tawfik said opposition MPs should have used the debate to scrutinise the RCI findings and hold the government accountable.
"The report concerns the interests of more than 10 million Tabung Haji depositors. Parliament is the best place for the opposition to expose weaknesses, question the government and demand accountability."
Muar MP Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman   criticised the walkout, saying MPs should remain in Parliament to scrutinise the RCI findings and protect depositors' interests rather than leave over the prime minister's absence.
Tawfik said walkouts could  be effective in certain circumstances, particularly in cases of serious breaches of parliamentary procedure,  questions over the legitimacy of proceedings, or where the move could affect quorum and force negotiations.
Such action, he said, should have a clear demand, a united front and a realistic  goal.
"Walkouts should be used as an exceptional tool, rather than a routine reaction."
POLITICAL THEATRE
Universiti Teknologi Malaysia Faculty of Social Sciences and Humanities associate professor Dr Mazlan Ali said the move was "political theatre" and  the prime minister's absence was not sufficient justification for leaving the House.
He said ministers were there to present and respond to the RCI report, while MPs had been given a chance to debate its findings.
"The report should first have been heard by the opposition MPs.
"In Parliament, there is no room for manipulation because everything presented and debated is recorded in the Hansard.
"Moreover, this concerns a report by a RCI. The government was prepared to present it through the minister in Parliament."
Mazlan said the walkout could undermine the opposition's role in providing checks and balances on the government.
"Opposition MPs should be there to scrutinise and question the government. If they are dissatisfied, they should ask questions and offer recommendations."
He said the move could also create the perception that the opposition was not taking the issue seriously.
Mazlan said walkouts could be justified when MPs were denied a fair opportunity to debate or when there was a serious dispute over parliamentary procedure.
"But in this case, the minister was present, the speaker had allowed the sitting to proceed and the government was prepared to answer questions. So why take that action?"
Mazlan said the move could ultimately backfire by shifting public attention away from the RCI findings and to  the opposition's conduct.
A PROTEST THAT STILL GETS  ATTENTION
However, International Islamic University Malaysia political analyst Associate Professor Dr Syaza Shukri said it would be wrong to dismiss the walkout as  ineffective.
She said while it had no direct impact on parliamentary proceedings, it had succeeded in drawing public attention to the opposition's objections.
"A walkout, or protests in general, is more about getting attention.
"In that sense, it works because it was widely reported and the opposition's reasons were also widely reported."
Syaza said the opposition might have had legitimate concerns about Anwar's absence and the timing of the RCI report's release, but the wider findings presented an opportunity for MPs to demand answers from the government.
"Maybe it would have been better if the prime minister was there, but the main thing he needs to answer is why the report was released now. The rest of the report is bigger than that.
"That was an opportunity for the opposition to ask questions and get answers."
Syaza also rejected the argument that the debate was less important because it did not require a vote.
"They are the opposition. Usually, for the opposition, debate and scrutiny are more important than voting because they do not have the numbers."
While Syaza acknowledged that MPs who walked out had missed an opportunity to question the government, she said the move was unlikely to significantly affect the opposition's credibility among its supporters.
Syaza said a walkout was more justified when MPs had exhausted other avenues of protest, particularly if the government prevented them from speaking or if remaining in the chamber could be seen as legitimising a controversial process.
"The difference with the walkout this time is that the opposition was not prevented from speaking.
"In fact, that was exactly what they were supposed to do."

Title: Parliamentary walkouts: When protest becomes the story
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The latest opposition walkout, this time over the  Royal Commission of Inquiry report on Tabung Haji, has exposed a familiar contradiction in  politics — the same tactic can be defended as a legitimate protest by one side and condemned as political theatre when used by the other.
This  was evident during the  Dewan Rakyat sitting, when most opposition members of parliament left  over Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's absence, while others, including Bersatu MPs, stayed to participate in the debate.
Jelutong MP R.S.N. Rayer criticised the walkout, saying opposition MPs should have remained to scrutinise the RCI findings.
"They could have made suggestions on how the mismanagement in Tabung Haji could be avoided, such as having the fund's annual financial reports tabled in Parliament," he said.
Rayer's stance echoed his criticism of a BN walkout in the Penang legislative assembly in 2009, when he said assemblymen should remain in the chamber to debate rather than "run away".
Bersatu MPs also rejected the latest walkout, with vice-president Datuk Dr Radzi Jidin saying the issue was too important to be overshadowed by "political drama".
Hi position is notable as he and other PN lawmakers staged a walkout in September 2023 after he was ordered to leave the Dewan Rakyat following a heated exchange with Anwar.
The latest walkout, however, was defended by Machang MP Wan Ahmad Fayhsal Wan Ahmad Kamal, who said the opposition was seeking a more thorough debate involving Anwar.
"We are not chickening out. We demand a more thorough representation, especially from the prime minister and finance minister himself."
He said the opposition had sought a deferment, not cancellation,  to allow Anwar to attend, and questioned why supporting materials, including 14 forensic audits, had not been tabled.
The contrasting positions are not new. Politicians on both sides had  defended and rejected walkouts depending on the circumstances, showing how the tactic can carry different  meaning.
In 2016, then opposition leader Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail defended PH MPs' walkout during the tabling of the 2017 Budget, saying  they wanted to "show emotions".
DAP's Teresa Kok also defended the tactic during the dispute  over proposed amendments to the Syariah Courts Act 1965, saying MCA MPs should have walked out to register their opposition.
In 2018, then opposition leader Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi defended a walkout over the appointment of the Dewan Rakyat speaker, while fellow Umno member Khairy Jamaluddin refused to join, saying "a walkout is not the way to protest".
The latest walkout also drew criticism from government lawmakers, who said MPs should use their time in the House to scrutinise the report.
Government Backbenchers Club  chairman Datuk Dr Zaliha Mustafa said the move was more of a  stunt than a principled stand.
"Even until today, we have yet to hear their  position on the TH RCI, an issue  concerning the interests of Muslims and Muslim pilgrims.
"MPs have a responsibility to remain engaged in Parliament, regardless of whether they are in government or opposition."
Pasir Gudang MP Hassan Abdul Karim also criticised the walkout, saying Pas and other PN MPs had missed a "golden opportunity" to demonstrate their commitment to protecting the interests of  Mal-ays and Muslims.
DAP's Kok said the walkout was unjustified and questioned the opposition's decision to focus its protest on Anwar's absence.
"When you walk out, you walk out with a strong reason. You walk out just because the prime minister is hospitalised... it is definitely not justifiable."
She said the walkout risked undermining the opposition's role as elected representatives.
Women, Family and Community Development Minister and Santubong MP Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said MPs who stayed had a valuable opportunity to speak for their constituents and raise concerns about the RCI findings.
She said the debate allowed MPs to put their views and concerns on record in the Hansard, while she had also used the opportunity to speak as an elected representative.
"Being an elected representative, we have our responsibility to the people. I did not want to miss that golden opportunity."

Title: Raja Muda of Selangor officiates opening of 2026 Sukma
Article:
SHAH ALAM: The opening ceremony of the 22nd Malaysia Games (Sukma) and Para Sukma 2026 was held at Dataran Kemerdekaan Shah Alam here last night.
The ceremony was officiated by the Raja Muda of Selangor, Tengku Amir Shah Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah.
Also present were Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari and Youth and Sports Minister Dr Mohammed Taufiq Johari, together with state government leaders and other dignitaries.
The latest edition of the Games will feature more than 5,000 young athletes from across the country competing for 468 gold medals in 37 sports until Aug 24.
Selangor last hosted the Games in 1998.
This edition also saw the Selangor government take measures to reduce costs, lowering the initial allocation of RM100 million to between RM40 million and RM50 million, in line with the decree of the Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah, for the Games to be organised prudently.
Sultan Sharafuddin had previously decreed that the hosting of Selangor Sukma 2026 should be postponed until the crisis in the Middle East was resolved and the redevelopment of Shah Alam Stadium was fully completed.
However, His Royal Highness later consented to the biennial Games being held on a prudent scale after granting an audience to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
Sarawak won the overall Sukma title in 2024 with 76 gold medals, one ahead of the second-placed Federal Territories, while Selangor finished third with 56 gold medals.
Last night's ceremony featured performances showcasing Selangor's identity, followed by the parade of contingents led by the Jalur Gemilang and state flags, as well as a speech by the Selangor Menteri Besar.
The ceremony concluded with the lighting of the Games torch in Shah Alam, marking the official start of the competition.

Title: University student loses RM29,000 in phone scam
Article:
IPOH: A 22-year-old university student lost RM29,000 after falling victim to a phone scam involving callers posing as a courier company representative and a law enforcement officer.
Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the victim received a call on July 31 from a caller posing as a delivery company representative, who claimed that a parcel containing prohibited items had been sent in his name.
He said the call was then transferred to another caller posing as a law enforcement officer, who accused the victim of being involved in money laundering.
"The victim was threatened with arrest and prosecution, causing him to panic and follow the syndicate's instructions.
"He was instructed to transfer RM8,999 to several bank accounts and place gold jewellery, including a necklace, rings, earrings and bracelet, worth about RM20,000 on the wall outside his house in Kampar," he said.
Alwi said the victim was told the cash and jewellery would be returned once the alleged investigation was completed.
However, he said the victim realised he had been cheated when neither the money nor jewellery was returned, prompting him to lodge a police report on Aug 1.
Following the report, the Commercial Crime Investigation Division of the Kampar police gathered intelligence and traced members of the syndicate.
Alwi said police conducted five raids at several locations in Petaling Jaya, Kelana Jaya, Hulu Kelang and Damansara, Kuala Lumpur, on Thursday.
"The raids resulted in the arrest of three men aged between 32 and 45.
"Police also seized eight SIM boxes, 11 Starlink units, 509 SIM cards, a laptop, two routers and five mobile phones," he said in a statement.
He said the communication equipment was believed to have been used by the syndicate as call gateways to facilitate communications for an online scam syndicate believed to be operating from overseas.
"The devices were also used to make it difficult for enforcement authorities to trace calls made by the online scam syndicate," he said.
Alwi said the three men had been remanded for four days from Aug 14 to 17 to assist investigations under Section 420 of the Penal Code.
He said those convicted under the provision could face imprisonment of between 1 and 10 years.
Alwi urged the public not to assist online scam syndicates, including by renting out residential premises or supplying communication equipment.
"Members of the public can channel information on activities linked to online scam syndicates to the nearest police station.
"Police will continue to take proactive action to curb activities involving such syndicates," he said.

Title: Two drivers held for blocking traffic to let supercar convoy pass
Article:
ISKANDAR PUTERI: Police have detained two car drivers believed to have acted as "marshals" by obstructing traffic to allow a luxury car convoy to pass at Bulatan Lebuh Kota Iskandar here.
Iskandar Puteri deputy police chief Superintendent Saifullah Jaya @ Yahaya said both men were detained yesterday by the district Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Division.
He said police began investigating after a video of the incident went viral on Threads at 6.16pm on Friday.
"Acting on a public complaint, the Iskandar Puteri District Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Division conducted an operation to trace the individuals involved.
"Investigations found that the supercar convoy was travelling from Puteri Harbour towards Johor Baru city centre, while the two drivers acted as marshals by stopping vehicles at the location to allow the convoy to pass," he said in a statement yesterday (Saturday).
Saifullah said the case was being investigated under Section 110 of the Road Transport Act 1987 for obstruction and interference offences, which carry a fine of up to RM1,000 upon conviction.
Four summonses were also issued for various offences involving non-compliance with vehicle specifications, while the vehicles involved were seized for further action.
He reminded the public that police would not compromise with individuals acting as unauthorised convoy escorts by obstructing traffic or stopping other road users without approval.
"Such actions clearly endanger themselves and other road users," he said.

Title: Penang remains under control after North Sumatra quake
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: The situation in Penang remains under control after tremors from a magnitude 6.4 earthquake in
North Sumatra, Indonesia
, were felt across the state this evening.
Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow urged the public to remain calm as authorities continued monitoring the situation.
"The situation is under control and no injuries have been reported so far," he said in a statement tonight.
Chow said the state government had received a report from the Penang Fire and Rescue Department's Operations Control Centre on the tremors following the earthquake in Indonesia.
He said the centre received public calls between 7.23pm and 7.27pm reporting tremors at nine locations across all five districts in Penang.
"Following the reports, the Fire and Rescue Department deployed its Operational Response Teams to the affected locations to conduct checks and monitoring," he added.
The operation involved 36 officers and personnel, nine vehicles and other equipment.
Chow advised the public to follow official information issued by the authorities.

Title: At least 47 dead in eastern Indonesia after magnitude 7.7 quake
Article:
JAKARTA: At least 47 people were killed after a magnitude 7.7 earthquake and dozens of aftershocks struck off eastern Indonesia on Saturday, the National Disaster Mitigation Agency (BNPB) said in its latest statement.
Rescue teams have yet to reach Nagekeo, the region closest to the epicentre, after landslides blocked roads and disrupted communications, officials said.
"The quake was massive, the shock was so strong," said Nona, a 51-year-old resident of Talibura, a village in East Nusa Tenggara. "There were 13 of us inside the house and we all ran to save ourselves."
Tsunami waves of less than 1 metre (3 feet) were recorded in several areas of the Southeast Asian nation after the early-morning quake. Authorities lifted a tsunami warning about three hours later.
Earlier, rescuers in the port town of Maumere found 20 dead, six injured and two people trapped under rubble, said Fathur Rahman, head of the city's rescue agency. Maumere is the main town in Sikka Regency on Flores Island in eastern Indonesia.
Suharyanto, head of the BNPB, earlier said residents remained trapped in several buildings across the affected area, while there were reports of landslides blocking a number of roads.
Teams have yet to reach Nagekeo and mobile communications in the region were affected, Fathur told Reuters earlier. Attempts to reach the area by road were thwarted by landslides, while another team was trying to reach it by ferry, he said.
About 2,000 residents in Nagekeo evacuated, and damage was reported to homes, warehouses and government buildings, the BNPB said. Authorities also reported power outages and traffic congestion in parts of the regency.
East Nusa Tenggara Governor Emanuel Melkiades Laka Lena told a press conference that at least five people were killed when buildings collapsed as they slept.
'WE DON'T DARE TO GO HOME'
Preliminary BNPB data showed 157 homes were heavily damaged, 41 moderately damaged and 148 lightly damaged. Damage was also reported at 87 schools, 18 health facilities, five places of worship and six office buildings, along with other infrastructure.
Parts of a building collapsed into dust and rubble as people screamed and ran in the street, according to a Facebook video, verified by Reuters as being filmed at a port in Maumere.
Rescuers were searching for survivors beneath a partially collapsed port building.
Siti Sulfia Bira, 37, who lives with her family near the port in Maumere, said she rushed to higher ground when the tremors started.
"At the moment we don't dare to go home just yet because the situation isn't stable, we still worry that there might be more tremors coming," she told Reuters.
Strong shaking was felt across East Nusa Tenggara, West Nusa Tenggara and parts of South Sulawesi, the BNPB said, with residents in several areas reporting tremors lasting about a minute.
"Most of the people felt the shock and scattered out of their homes," the agency said.
A hospital in Ende district in East Nusa Tenggara was moving patients outside, Kompas TV footage showed, while Kompas.com reported at least one landslide.
Indonesian geophysics agency BMKG recorded the first quake at 4.58am (2158 GMT) at a depth of 15km (9 miles), followed by several aftershocks.
The BMKG said the same area was hit by a magnitude 7.5 earthquake in 1992 that caused extensive destruction.
Australia's tsunami warning centre said the undersea quake posed "no tsunami threat to the Australian mainland, islands or territories."
Indonesia straddles the "Pacific Ring of Fire", a seismically active zone where tectonic plates meet, triggering frequent earthquakes and volcanic eruptions.
In 2018, a magnitude 7.5 earthquake and tsunami struck the city of Palu on Sulawesi island, killing more than 4,000 people.

Title: No damage, casualties after earthquake tremors felt at nine Penang premises
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: No damage or casualties were reported after tremors from a magnitude 6.4 earthquake in North Sumatra were felt at nine premises across Penang tonight.
Penang Fire and Rescue Department assistant director of operations John Sagun Francis said checks carried out at all nine locations found no incidents or hazards.
"There were no incidents reported at the locations.
"Our personnel conducted checks and monitoring to ensure the areas were safe and free from any other hazards," he said.
The locations comprised condominiums, apartments, flats, a hotel and an industrial facility.
John said on Penang island, checks were carried out at Baystar Condominium and One Precinct in the southwest district, as well as Apartment Manggis, Summer Place Condominium and Apartment Pelangi Gate on Lebuh Macallum in the northeast district.
On the mainland, firemen inspected Pacific Megamall flats in Seberang Perai Tengah, Marminton Homes and Crowne Plaza Hotel in Seberang Perai Utara, and the TF-AMD facility in Batu Kawan, Seberang Perai Selatan.
"We received calls through the MERS 999 emergency system between 7.23pm and 7.27pm, prompting teams from six fire stations to be deployed.
"A total of 36 personnel, supported by four fire rescue tenders, two light fire rescue tenders and three Emergency Medical Rescue Services vehicles, were involved in the operation," he added.
The operation ended about 10.40pm after the teams completed their checks and found the areas safe.
The earthquake struck North Sumatra at 6.54pm today, with tremors reported in parts of Peninsular Malaysia.
MetMalaysia said the earthquake was centred 37km southwest of Pematangsiantar at a depth of 154km, with no tsunami threat to Malaysia.

Title: NST Leader: Is 'cash for stray dogs' the right approach?
Article:
"CASH for stray dogs" should not become a false choice between protecting public safety and protecting animal welfare. Both objectives are legitimate.
The real question is whether a cash bounty is the most effective and responsible way to achieve them.
Granted, local councils have a duty to address dangerous stray animals, but the method adopted must command public confidence, minimise unintended consequences and uphold professional standards.
Although there aren't any official figures about the number of stray dogs in Negri Sembilan, the "cash for stray dogs" plan sure reads like an act of desperation.
Last year, the then menteri besar said there were thousands of stray dogs in the state. Have they grown into tens of thousands? Or more?
Be that as it may, we fear that dishing out cash per captured dog may create perverse incentives. One  is the risk of pets being mistaken for strays, which  animal rights groups call "pet capture".
Another is that RM50 per adult stray and RM25 for younger ones will induce the public to prioritise quantity over humane handling of the animals.
Veterinarians have warned that capturing stray dogs, especially those that are infected with disease, could be dangerous for the untrained public. It is best left to trained personnel, particularly where safety and welfare are concerned.
Local councils are best suited for this, but if the mistreatment of stray animals by them in the past is any guide, then one needs to ask if they have sufficient safeguards in place.
This is especially so for the local councils in Negri Sembilan now that they have introduced the "cash for strays" scheme. Do they have a verification system to ensure that the captured animals are genuinely strays? Do they have a system to read microchips? Have they put in place procedures to prevent abuse of the scheme?
Animal welfare groups have consistently warned against treating rescue as the problem. It is not.
It is just a symptom of many underlying causes. State authorities and local councils have missed this by a mile by focusing on reactive approaches. One animal welfare group, Persatuan Haiwan Terbiar Malaysia (SAFM), told this newspaper last month that stray animal management must instead be preventive, humane and community-based.
According to SAFM, many animals end up in the streets because owners neglect their responsibilities or abandon them when caring for them becomes inconvenient.
The welfare group's view is that only a structured and sustainable approach can guarantee stray animal welfare.
For this to happen there must be responsible adoption, post-adoption accountability, spaying, vaccination support through veterinary professionals, greater awareness of pet licensing, anti-cruelty education and greater community participation.
Pet ownership isn't a temporary pledge; it's a lifetime commitment.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: US says more oil is leaving Hormuz, but the numbers don't add up
Article:
JUST how much crude oil is leaving the Strait of Hormuz? United States Energy Secretary Chris Wright claims that almost nine million barrels per day, but the companies that track vessel movements say, at best, it is about half this volume.
The amount of crude leaving the Middle East via the narrow chokepoint matters, as it's this oil that goes to Asia, the top energy-consuming region that has been hardest hit by the fallout since the US and Israel attacked Iran on Feb 28.
Wright said on  X on Wednesday  that "thanks to the coordinated efforts of the US military and our gulf allies, the seven-day average for oil leaving the Strait of Hormuz is currently up to almost nine million bpd".
He further said that adding in an "additional 5-7 million bpd leaving the region via newly upgraded pipelines and export facilities, total oil flows are currently averaging approximately 15 million bpd".
This would take total exports from the Middle East to around 75 per cent of the volumes prior to the start of the conflict.
The problem is that Wright's numbers don't tally with those provided by several vessel tracking services.
Wright didn't specify the exact time period for his seven-day average, but data from commodity analysts Kpler shows crude exports via  Hormuz for the week beginning July 27 at 2.77 million bpd.
This drops to 1.74 million bpd for the week beginning Aug 3, and even the best week since the start of the conflict saw only 6.98 million bpd leave in the seven days starting June 29.
What of total exports from the Middle East?
This would include cargoes leaving from Saudi Arabia's Yanbu port in the Red Sea, as well as shipments from Oman and the Fujairah facility in the United Arab Emirates.
Kpler data shows crude shipments of 9.53 million bpd in the week beginning Aug 3, and a  four-week average of 12.26 million bpd.
Data from LSEG Oil Research — filtered to show only cargoes that are being loaded, have been loaded, are underway or have been discharged —  shows Middle East crude exports of 9.33 million bpd for the first 12 days of August, down from 12.35 million bpd last month.
The tracking data shows total exports from the Middle East are still well below pre-conflict levels, with Kpler data showing shipments of 18.7 million bpd in the three months until the end of February.
If Wright's numbers are accurate, it would also be logical for import data to show rising arrivals from the Middle East.
There was a spike in crude imports from the Middle East last month, with Kpler showing arrivals of 13.27 million bpd, of which 10.86 million bpd was discharged at Asian ports.
This was up from the 9.26 million bpd of imports from the Middle East in April, which was the lowest in Kpler data going back to 2013, but last month's  number was still well short of the 18.71 million bpd average for the three months leading up to the start of the Iran war.
The July number was also because a large number of tankers managed to exit Hormuz during the ceasefire between the US and Iran, which lasted for about three weeks after it was struck in mid-June.
What the vessel-tracking data shows is a gap of between three and five million bpd between what they can see and what Wright says is being shipped from the Middle East.
There are three main possibilities to explain the gap.
THE
numbers provided by Wright and his department are correct and the tracking services are missing some clandestine shipments that are being done out of sight.
WRIGHT
and his department genuinely believe their numbers, but they are miscounting shipments.
WRIGHT
knows his numbers are inaccurate but disseminates the information anyway because it suits the political narrative of his boss, President Donald Trump, who is trying to spin that the war is going well.
The third possibility is more disturbing, and doubts will remain as long as Wright does not provide evidence, especially given the Trump administration's track record of misinformation, inaccurate claims and delusional thinking about the state of the conflict.
The writer is from Reuters

Title: Stray dogs spark safety fears in Kajang village
Article:
KAJANG: Residents of Kampung Sungai Sekamat are concerned over the growing number of stray dogs roaming the area, with some fearing for the safety of children and students.
According to a report by Buletin TV3, residents said nearly 30 stray dogs were roaming the neighbourhood, particularly from evening into the night, with the problem persisting for almost 5 years.
The dogs were frequently seen near a playground and cemetery, as well as along a route used by children travelling to and from school.
Resident Nur Adibah Nasrudin said she was involved in an accident after hitting a dog while riding her motorcycle to pick up her sister from school.
"I saw the dog, and it appeared to move aside, but it suddenly came back into the middle of the road. I couldn't avoid it and hit it," she said.
The incident heightened concerns among residents over the risks posed by dogs roaming the roads.
Residents also complained that the dogs scavenged through rubbish bins, left droppings around the neighbourhood and occasionally entered homes.
Another resident raised concerns over the risk of rabies and urged the authorities to act before a serious incident occurred.
"We don't want to wait until someone dies before the relevant parties take action," she said.
Residents called on the local authorities to strengthen enforcement and take more effective measures to manage the stray dog population.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Woman who died after headscarf entangled in floodgate roller was on duty
Article:
SABAK BERNAM: Police have confirmed that the Drainage and Irrigation Department (DID) worker found dead at a floodgate near a hotel here this afternoon was on duty at the time.
District police chief Superintendent Md Yusof Ahmad said the 55-year-old woman worked as a DID floodgate operator in Sabak Bernam.
"The victim was at the location to close the floodgate following a high tide.
"However, an accident occurred, resulting in the woman's death," he said when contacted.
Md Yusof said police received a report on the incident about 4pm.
He said the body was taken to Hospital Tengku Ampuan Jemaah  Sabak Bernam for a post-mortem to determine the cause of death.
The case has been classified as sudden death.
Earlier, it was reported that
the victim died
after her headscarf became entangled in the floodgate roller today.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department Operations Division assistant director Ashrul Riezal Asbar was reported to have said that the department received a distress call at 3.35pm.
He said a team of five firefighters from the Sabak Bernam Fire and Rescue Station rushed to the scene.

Title: S. Korea's blind fortune-tellers could not see AI coming
Article:
CLIENTS  have drifted away from Song Oh-soon's fortune-telling village on the edge of Seoul, preferring online artificial intelligence-powered divination to the centuries-old prophesying tradition still practiced there.
At 86, Song is one of the last members of a community of visually impaired practitioners that drew generations of South Koreans seeking answers and advice about everything from illness and money to love and fate.
In one of the world's most AI-connected societies, the village's greatest challenge is not fading belief in fortune-telling, but the way it is consumed.
Song remains adamantly offline, relying on the "Four Pillars of Destiny" astrology in Braille and on her four decades of experience in careful listening —  a skill her automated competition cannot match.
"There were people who came here wanting to die," Song said in northern Seoul's Mia village. "I persuaded them to keep living."
"I also once wanted to die, but I found this work and survived."
Today, silence is often Song's only visitor. The community was once home to 70 or 80 practitioners, but fewer than 20 remain.
Many have died. Their shops down narrow alleys sit dark behind faded signs advertising "traditional fortune-telling houses".
"When I go outside for a walk, it's quiet," Song said in her tiny room that serves as both home and consulting space. "It feels lonely."
Figures show South Korea's fortune-telling business is growing — worth 1.4 trillion won as of 2024, according to start-up analysis firm InnoForest.
Many now turn to mobile apps and AI chatbots such as ChatGPT and Gemini for readings, a survey by market researcher Embrain said this year.
Occasionally, though, someone still seeks out a human intervention.
University professor Oh Ji-hye for years walked past the village without going inside, opting instead for AI readings during her commute.
Only recently, anxious about her career, did she turn to Song for a phone consultation.
"It felt good that someone rather than AI was concentrating on and listening to my story," the 44-year-old said.
Mia village emerged in 1966 after the first blind fortune-teller settled there, according to the Seongbuk Cultural Centre, which researches the district's history.
As Seoul boomed in the 1970s and 1980s, the neighbourhood enjoyed cheap rents and a constant foot traffic of potential customers by the time Song arrived in 1984.
She lost her sight in a childhood illness before the Korean War and by 11 was studying Korean fortune-telling —  predicting subjects' futures based on their birth dates and times.
She was a professional by 16, working in an industry where many people with disabilities,   especially women, have been historically confined owing to discrimination.
"Nowadays, if a visually impaired person is musically talented, they can pursue a career in music," she said.
"But back when I lost my sight, there was nothing else I could do besides this job."
Over her lifetime, South Korea has witnessed the devastation of the 1950-53 war, periods of military rule and the 1990s financial crisis.
After periods of hardship and loss, the nation has emerged as a global financial powerhouse — with recent astronomical profits from manufacturing AI microchips.
Those gains have lifted the nation's fortunes. Clients who once came for advice about medical ailments can now head to hospital instead.
But the technology has drawn away clients from Song's 50,000-won sessions in favour of free or affordable AI readings.
Most of the remaining practitioners have little online presence, and many cannot be found through major search platforms.
"I don't think people are less interested in fortune-telling," Song said. "But these days, they look online, so they do not come all the way to us."
Despite the village's decline, Song believes no fate is set in stone.
"If you put in the effort and make wise judgments, good fortune will come your way three times in your life," she said.
The writer is from AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sultan Nazrin graces National Month programme in Perak
Article:
IPOH: Sultan of Perak Sultan Nazrin Muizzuddin Shah today graced a programme aimed at instilling loyalty to the King and country in conjunction with National Month 2026.
Perak Education Department director Zulkafli Mohamed Mokhtar said participation in the programme had increased by 15 per cent from the previous year, reflecting its growing significance as a platform to nurture students' talents, confidence and potential.
He said the programme had a significant impact not only on students' physical development but also on shaping their thinking, values and future, in line with the Malaysia Education Plan (RPM) 2026-2035.
Zulkafli said the programme also supported Perak's education vision of producing students who were not only academically excellent but also possessed good character, critical thinking skills and a strong patriotic spirit.
He said students should be encouraged to appreciate the nation's history and heritage while being equipped with the skills to become credible leaders in the future.
"This is the generation of future custodians expected to safeguard the continuity of independence and uphold the sovereignty of the King and country, ensuring a future for Malaysia that remains peaceful, prosperous and glorious," he said.
Zulkafli said 2028 would mark a historic milestone for Perak with the celebration of the 500th anniversary of the Perak Sultanate.
"Five centuries of the Perak Sultanate are not merely a chapter in history, but a symbol of the continuity of the monarchy, sovereignty, heritage and identity of the people of Perak, which have been preserved and passed down to this day.
"Indeed, an appreciation of history shapes identity, while a strong identity produces a generation capable of safeguarding the heritage and sovereignty of the state and nation," he said.
At the event, Sultan Nazrin presented the Special Award for Best Achievement by a District Education Office to the Kinta Utara District Education Office, which received RM20,000.
He also presented prizes to winners of the English Language Public Speaking Competition and Bahasa Melayu Public Speaking Competition in the primary, lower secondary and upper secondary categories.
Meanwhile, Raja Permaisuri Perak Tuanku Zara Salim presented prizes to winners of the essay writing and poetry writing competitions in the primary, lower secondary and upper secondary categories.
Also present were Deputy Education Minister Wong Kah Woh and Perak Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad.

Title: Police probe FB account over alleged sedition, insults against royal institution
Article:
CHUKAI: Police are investigating the owner of the Facebook account 'Ahmad Mu'min' over a post suspected of containing elements of sedition and insulting the royal institution, the Malaysian government and the police.
Kemaman district police chief Superintendent Mohd Razi Mohd Rosli said the investigation under Section 4(1) of the Sedition Act 1948 and Section 233 of the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 was launched after a report was lodged by a 29-year-old man at 11.14am today.
"The police will investigate the identity of the account owner and subsequently conduct an investigation in accordance with legal procedures," he said in a statement today.
He said the latest post on the Facebook account, among other things, alleged that police officers had kicked a motorcyclist during a joint operation at Pantai Penunjuk, Kijal, near here, about 6.30pm yesterday.
"The allegation that police officers kicked one of the motorcyclists is baseless, as can be seen in a recording that went viral on social media.
"The statement was malicious, and the public is urged to verify the content of any post that has the potential to incite hatred against the police," he said.
He added that the operation was carried out following public complaints about illegal racing activities that were disturbing public order.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'We thought we were dizzy,' says Penang resident as tremors also felt in Perak
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A magnitude 6.4 earthquake struck northern Sumatra, Indonesia, at 6.54pm today, the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) said.
MetMalaysia said the earthquake was centred at 2.9 degrees north and 98.8 degrees east, at a depth of 154km, about 37km southwest of Pematangsiantar.
It said tremors were felt along parts of the west coast of Peninsular Malaysia, but there was no tsunami threat to the country.
In Penang, state Fire and Rescue Department director Mohamad Shoki Hamzah said
the departmen
t received nine emergency calls regarding the tremors about 6.55pm.
He said the calls involved four areas in two districts on the island, as well as several areas in Seberang Perai.
"Our personnel have gone to the locations and are conducting further inspections," he said when contacted.
The tremors, which lasted several minutes, were reportedly felt in areas including Sungai Baru, Bayan Baru, George Town, Jelutong, Tanjung Bungah, Batu Ferringhi and Air Itam on the island, as well as Perai, Bagan, Teluk Air Tawar, Jalan Baru, Bukit Mertajam, Kepala Batas and Bertam in Seberang Perai.
A Bagan resident, Syahirah Mokhtar, 45, said she was initially startled when she felt the tremors at home before contacting her child in Pantai Robina, Bagan, who also experienced the tremors.
She said the tremors lasted about two to three minutes, with water in a cup placed on the table visibly moving. She then went downstairs and found that many other residents of the apartment had also done so.
"Many residents initially did not realise that the tremors were caused by an earthquake because they thought they were feeling dizzy.
"But some noticed that the hanging lights and ceiling fans in their homes were swaying, so we all decided to go downstairs because we were worried that something might happen," she said.
Social media posts indicated that tremors were also felt in Perak, including areas around Kuala Kangsar, Alor Pongsu, Bagan Serai, Teluk Intan, Ulu Kinta, Meru and Ipoh.
"Even Ulu Kinta felt the shaking…," a social media user posted, while another reported feeling the same tremors in Kuala Kangsar.
Meanwhile, Perak Fire and Rescue Department Operations Division assistant director Sabarodzi Nor Ahmad told Bernama when contacted that the department had yet to receive any emergency calls related to the incident.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Tiny Tun Ms and Siti Hasmahs steal the spotlight
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Young lookalikes of former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad and his wife, Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohd Ali, charmed the crowd at a costume contest held to mark his 101st birthday.
The contest, dubbed the 'Cosplay Parade', was held during the Mahathir 101: Piknik Legasi event at Taman Lagenda today, with children recreating the couple's signature looks and outfits.
Event organiser Muhammad Alif Aiman Azman said the contest was initially open to both adults and children, but only entries for the children's category were received.
"It was a Tun Dr Mahathir and Tun Siti Hasmah lookalike contest, where participants mimicked the duo's signature styles," he told the New Straits Times.
Alif said 15 children took part, with two boys dressed as Mahathir and 13 girls as Siti Hasmah.
Five winners were selected, with the contest judged by Mahathir's eldest daughter, Datin Paduka Marina Mahathir, and a Langkawi local who preferred to be identified as Kak Yong.
View on Threads
A video shared on Threads by @amofficialmy earlier showing the young participants in their outfits quickly caught users' attention.
"The first one's styling is so cute. She just forgot the spectacles," one user said.
Another said the girls showed "great potential", while another described the scene as "cuteness overload".
The four-hour event featured a public picnic-themed potluck to mark Mahathir's 101st birthday and commemorate his legacy in Langkawi's development.
More than 1,000 people attended the event, which also featured a podcast session with Mahathir, a colouring contest, exhibitions and vendors.
Mahathir, who served as Langkawi member of parliament from 2018 to 2022, celebrated his 101st birthday on July 10.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Audit findings crucial to strengthening public sector accountability, says AG
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The National Audit Department is carrying out its mandate as the country's audit institution independently, professionally and with integrity to strengthen accountability, transparency and governance in the public sector, says Auditor General Datuk Seri Wan Suraya Wan Mohd Radzi.
She said audit findings were compiled in the Auditor General's Report (LKAN), an important instrument in the country's checks-and-balances mechanism.
Wan Suraya said the Auditor General's role in providing opinions on financial statements and making audit recommendations was not merely to fulfil reporting requirements to Parliament, but more importantly, to encourage effective corrective action and improvements in public sector management.
"Through the LKAN, weaknesses and non-compliance can be identified, corrective action can be taken, and systems and governance can be strengthened.
"The ultimate goal is to ensure public funds are managed and spent prudently and transparently, while delivering the appropriate value and benefits to the people," she said in her speech at the 2026 Auditor General's Cup Debate Competition (PKAN 2026).
The competition carries the theme "120 Years of the National Audit Department: Driving Accountability, Building an Integrity-Driven MADANI Generation".
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sarawak wants transboundary haze issue tackled at Asean level
Article:
KUCHING: The transboundary haze issue in Sarawak should continue to be discussed at the Asean level through the Sub-Regional Ministerial Steering Committee on Transboundary Haze Pollution to find effective solutions to minimise its impact.
Sarawak Deputy Premier Datuk Amar Douglas Uggah Embas said the Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Ministry, which represents Malaysia on the committee, would put forward proposals to address the issue.
"We need to be cautious because areas such as Kuala Baram, if affected by forest fires, could cause smoke to drift and affect Brunei.
"As such, related matters will be discussed by the committee before being referred to the relevant ministries.
"The ministry will raise the issues and challenges we face and seek solutions to reduce their impact," he told reporters after the state-level Handicraft Competition prize presentation here today.
Uggah, who is also Sarawak State Disaster Management Committee chairman, said the state had submitted an application for a cloud seeding operation and was assessing the most suitable timing for its implementation.
Yesterday, Uggah said cloud seeding was being considered to address prolonged hot and dry weather conditions, which could affect water sources and worsen haze conditions in several areas.
Transboundary haze has affected several areas in Sarawak since Aug 8 due to prevailing wind patterns carrying smoke from hotspots in neighbouring regions into the state.
Areas that recorded Air Pollutant Index readings at the very unhealthy level were Kuching, Samarahan, Sri Aman, Sarikei, Sibu, Bintulu, Samalaju and Miri.

Title: Sign language opens doors to Islamic learning for Kelantan deaf community
Article:
KOTA BARU: For members of the Kelantan Deaf Association, hearing impairment is no barrier to learning the basics of Islam, with about 100 members attending Fardu Ain classes twice a month to deepen their understanding of religious teachings.
The latest class was held at Balai Islam in Lundang here on Friday from 10am to noon.
The classes use a simple but effective approach, with religious officers from the Kelantan Islamic Religious Affairs Department delivering lessons through normal speech while a sign language interpreter translates the teachings for participants.
Association sign language interpreter Noor Haseken P. Rameli said the programme had been conducted for several years and was held twice a month free of charge.
"The classes provide an opportunity for our members to learn and better understand matters related to their faith in a way that is accessible to them.
"The lessons are conducted manually, with the interpreter translating what the religious officer explains into sign language," she said.
Participant Rohani Johari, 42, said the classes were something she looked forward to as they allowed her to learn alongside fellow members of the deaf community.
"I am very happy to be able to attend these classes. I can learn more about Fardu Ain and practise what I learn in my daily life," said the mother of eight, who works at a car wash centre.
Another participant, housewife Muzlizah Mustafa, 38, said the classes had helped her gain a better understanding of religious matters.
"I am happy to be here because we can learn together and ask questions through the interpreter," said the mother of an 11-year-old daughter.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MCMC boosts UTeM's digital connectivity, benefiting more than 12,000 students
Article:
ALOR GAJAH: More than 12,000 students at Universiti Teknikal Malaysia Melaka (UTeM) are benefiting from upgraded digital infrastructure, including 410 Wi-Fi access points (APs) and a new 4G communications tower at the university.
The Universal Service Provision (USP) project, implemented by the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC), is expected to strengthen connectivity across the campus, particularly to support learning, teaching and training under the Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) system.
MCMC said 108 of the 410 planned APs had been operational since June 2025 under Phase 2 of the Public Institution of Higher Learning Wi-Fi Project, while an additional 302 APs were being installed under Phase 3, scheduled for completion on Sept 23.
"The new 4G communications tower is also being developed within the UTeM campus and is expected to be completed in November.
"It will help strengthen communications coverage while improving the quality and user experience of digital services among the campus community," MCMC said in a statement today.
Earlier, MCMC Southern Region senior director Rizal Abd Malek, representing Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil, inspected the implementation of the project at UTeM.
He was accompanied by UTeM deputy vice-chancellor (Academic and International) Professor Dr Mohd Rizal Salleh and deputy vice-chancellor (Student Affairs and Alumni) Associate Professor Datuk Dr Sabri Mohd Sharif.
MCMC said stable, fast and high-capacity internet access was essential at UTeM as a technical university, particularly to support smart laboratories, cloud-based engineering software, digital simulations and various learning applications forming part of the modern TVET ecosystem.
"The upgrade will also create a more conducive learning environment, while enabling students and educators to utilise digital technology more effectively in the teaching and learning process," it said.
The initiative is also part of the Communications Ministry's ongoing efforts, through MCMC, to strengthen digital connectivity at public higher education institutions in line with current educational needs and rapid technological development.
MCMC said improved connectivity at educational institutions would not only facilitate access to learning resources, but also help equip students with digital skills and experience relevant to industry requirements.
The digital infrastructure upgrade at UTeM is expected to further strengthen the country's TVET ecosystem, enhance graduates' readiness to adapt to technological changes and support the development of digital and technical talent needed to drive future economic growth.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] North Sumatra quake sends tremors across several parts of Penang
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Tremors from a magnitude 6.4 earthquake in North Sumatra, Indonesia, were felt in several parts of Penang this evening, with five reports received by authorities.
The Fire and Rescue Department confirmed receiving five reports of tremors, four from Penang island and one from the mainland.
The earthquake occurred at 6.54pm, with its epicentre located about 6km from Pematangsiantar City in North Sumatra.
Penang Fire and Rescue Department assistant director of operations John Sagun Francis, when contacted, confirmed that five reports had been received so far.
"Four of the reports are from the island, involving both the northeast and southwest districts. Another is from the mainland.
"Firefighters were dispatched to the reported locations after receiving the reports," he added.
No injuries or damage have been reported in Penang so far.
Social media users also reported feeling tremors in Balik Pulau, Batu Ferringhi, Tanjung Tokong, Straits Quay, Bayan Lepas, Macallum, Air Itam, Teluk Kumbar, Greenlane, Jelutong, Bukit Mertajam and Butterworth.
Elriena Natasha said she felt tremors in Batu Ferringhi about 6.55pm, while Ivy Tan shared video footage showing lights swaying in Pulau Andaman.
Meanwhile, the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) confirmed that a magnitude 6.4 earthquake had struck northern Sumatra, Indonesia.
It said the earthquake was centred at 2.9 degrees north and 98.8 degrees east, at a depth of 154km, about 37km southwest of Pematangsiantar.
MetMalaysia also confirmed that tremors were felt along parts of the west coast of Peninsular Malaysia, but there was no tsunami threat to the country.
Authorities are continuing to monitor the situation and assess further reports of tremors or damage.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Several Sepang roads to close for Sukma cycling event
Article:
SEPANG: Several major roads in the Sepang district will be closed and traffic diverted in stages from tomorrow until Aug 19 in conjunction with the Selangor Malaysia Games (Sukma) cycling event.
District police chief Assistant Commissioner Norhizam Bahaman said 96 locations in the district would be monitored for traffic control throughout the event.
"The traffic control duties will be divided into four zones, namely Zone A, covering Jalan Pantai Sepang Putra to the Tumbuk border; Zone B, Jalan Dengkil-Jenderam Hulu; Zone C, Jalan Jenderam-Salak; and Zone D, Jalan Salak Sepang-Sungai Pelek.
"All roads involved will be closed in stages from 8.30am to 12.30pm," he said in a statement today.
Norhizam said personnel from the Sepang district police headquarters' Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Division, local authority enforcement officers and traffic personnel from the Selangor police headquarters would be stationed at road junctions and traffic lights.
He said police would also conduct patrols and monitor the affected areas to ensure safety and smooth traffic flow.
On Aug 16, 17 and 19, roads scheduled for phased closures from 8.30am to 12.30pm include Jalan Bukit Bangkong-Tanjung Rhu, Persiaran Pantai Sepang Putra, Jalan Kampung Bagan Lalang and Jalan Tumbuk Sempadan.
Meanwhile, the Aug 18 road closures will involve 18 locations, including Persiaran Pantai Sepang Putra, Jalan Kampung Bagan Lalang, Jalan Bukit Bangkong-Tanjung Rhu, Jalan Tumbuk Sempadan, Jalan Banting-Semenyih (Dengkil-bound) and the Pekan Dengkil traffic lights.

Title: KDM rep attends GRS assemblymen's programme amid support withdrawal
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Parti Kesejahteraan Demokratik Masyarakat (KDM) sole elected representative Datuk Rusdin Rimad attended a programme with other Gabungan Rakyat Sabah (GRS) assemblymen here this morning, amid his party's announcement that it was withdrawing its support for the coalition.
GRS secretary-general Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali said he had contacted the Paginatan assemblyman following
KDM acting president Priscella Peter's
announcement that the party was withdrawing its support for GRS.

Title: Flores earthquake: 16 Malaysian tourists safe, says embassy
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A group of 16 Malaysian tourists who were in areas affected by a magnitude 7.7 earthquake on Flores Island in East Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia, were confirmed safe and in good health.
In a media advisory on Saturday, the Foreign Ministry said the Malaysian Embassy in Jakarta had established contact with the group following the earthquake, which struck northeast of Mbay in Nagekeo Regency at 4.58am local time.
"At this stage, the ministry can confirm that there have been no reports of Malaysians affected by this incident.
"Furthermore, the embassy has successfully established contact with a group of 16 Malaysian tourists known to be in the vicinity, all of whom have been confirmed to be safe and in good health," the advisory said.
The ministry said the embassy was actively coordinating with the relevant local authorities to ascertain the safety and well-being of Malaysians in the affected areas.
It advised Malaysians residing in or travelling to the affected regions to remain vigilant, prioritise their personal safety and strictly adhere to safety instructions issued by local authorities.
"The ministry will continue to monitor the situation closely and provide updates should there be any new developments concerning Malaysian citizens," the advisory read.
Malaysians were also urged to register and regularly update their contact details through the e-Konsular portal to facilitate timely communication and consular assistance.
Those requiring immediate consular assistance or facing emergencies may contact the Malaysian Embassy in Jakarta via its emergency helpline at +6281380813036 or email mwjakarta@kln.gov.my.
