Title: From rice to remedy: Penang maker’s time‑honoured 40‑day method keeps traditional ‘bedak sejuk’ craft alive
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 16 — Before commercial talcum powders and skincare products became commonplace,
bedak sejuk
was a familiar household staple, used to cool the skin in Malaysia’s hot and humid weather and to soothe the itchiness associated with conditions such as chicken pox.
Made simply from rice and water, the traditional cooling powder was once prepared at home for personal use.
Children and adults alike would often be seen with the white streaks it left on their faces and bodies after being mixed with water and applied to the skin.
Over the years, however,
bedak sejuk
gradually fell out of favour, often regarded as an old-fashioned product used mainly by older generations.
But in recent years, traditional
bedak sejuk
has begun to regain popularity, helped by greater public interest in heritage products, according to maker Yeoh Siong Huat.
The 49-year-old took over Bedak Sejuk Lean Seng from his father in 2016 and now supplies retailers and shops across Penang.
“The method of making
bedak sejuk
has been handed down for generations, but it used to be made at home for personal use until my parents began selling it about 50 years ago,” he said.
Yeoh said his parents had previously operated a small-scale business rearing pigs while also producing
belacan
and
bedak sejuk
for sale.
“When they first started selling
bedak sejuk
, many families were still making their own at home because it was easy to prepare using only rice and water,” he said.
Business gradually improved over the years, and Yeoh stepped in to take over the operation about a decade ago as his parents grew older.
His father died just a year later, leaving Yeoh to continue the craft largely on his own, with occasional help from his brothers on weekends.
Although rice is the only ingredient, making
bedak sejuk
is a slow and labour-intensive process involving several stages.
“The first step is to wash the rice and soak it for a month. Every week, I have to change the water or it will spoil,” he said.
After a month, the rice is washed and rinsed again before being blended into a paste.
The paste is then strained and left to drip dry for between eight and nine hours.
“Once it has dried, I can form the granules. Each batch contains more than 900 granules,” he said.
The granules being dried under the sun. — Picture courtesy of Penang Global Tourism
The granules are arranged in rows on trays and dried under direct sunlight for three days, with at least three hours of sunshine needed each day.
The process is highly dependent on the weather.
“If it is the rainy season, I have to wait for sunny days to dry the granules. If it rains for too many days, the batch may grow mould and I would have to discard it and start all over again,” he said.
Once fully dried, Yeoh uses a fan to remove dust before sieving the granules again to separate out crushed pieces and powder.
The finished granules are then bottled and sent to retailers.
“I have sent my products for laboratory testing to ensure the quality remains good and that they are safe for use on the skin,” he said.
Yeoh packs about 100 bottles a day, but completing a single batch can take at least 40 days, sometimes longer, depending on the weather.
Yeoh packs about 100 bottles a day, but completing a single batch can take at least 40 days. — Picture courtesy of Penang Global Tourism
Traditionally used as part of a skincare routine,
bedak sejuk
continues to be used in much the same way today.
Each bottle retails for RM8, which Yeoh said brings in only enough revenue to cover costs and provide him with a modest living.
“I continue doing this because it is a traditional craft passed down by our ancestors that should be preserved,” he said.
“It is a lot of work and hard labour, and I am definitely not becoming rich from it,” he added.
Yeoh is single so he hoped that his nephews or nieces may one day be interested in taking over the business in future.

Title: Fire dept calls for systematic measures to prevent fallen tree incidents nationwide
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 16 — Incidents of fallen trees in Malaysia can no longer be considered isolated incidents that only occur during the rainy season; instead, they require a preventive approach that is more systematic through regular safety audits, inter-agency data sharing and consistent maintenance.
Malaysian Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) statistics show that 26,001 cases of fallen trees were recorded nationwide from 2021 to June, last year, resulting in 50 fatalities and 243 injuries.
Its director-general, Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad said that emergency calls related to fallen trees remain consistently high, ranging between 4,400 and 5,200 cases per year, while for the first half of 2026 alone, 1,912 cases were recorded.
“During that period, the incident of fallen trees resulted in 50 deaths and 243 injuries, while 360 victims were successfully rescued without injuries.
“This data shows that although the number of cases has not consistently increased, the occurrence of fallen trees still poses a serious risk to public safety,” he told
Bernama.
The media had reported that the Maran Umno Youth chief was among the four who perished in a fallen tree incident on Jalan Lama Bentong heading towards the Janda Baik entrance, Bentong, on Aug 3. On July 19, a 43-year-old man died after the car he was driving was crushed by a fallen tree near the Singapore Embassy on Jalan Tun Razak, Kuala Lumpur.
Nor Hisham said that among the main factors identified as causing tree falls are thunderstorms accompanied by strong winds and heavy rain, especially during the monsoon transition phase.
Continuous rain can cause the soil to become saturated and reduce the stability of the tree’s root system, thereby increasing the risk of the tree falling.
“In addition to weather factors, the physical condition of the trees such as old, diseased, decayed trees or those with weak root and branch structures also contribute to the occurrence,” he said.
A recent investigation by the Penang City Council found that the cause of the 90-year-old angsana tree that fell on Jalan Macalister, Penang, on Aug 3 was due to rotting roots, cavities at the base of the trunk, chronic soil compaction and limited root space.
“JBPM views that tree falls are usually not caused by a single factor, but rather involve a combination of various factors including weather, the physical condition of the tree, and the level of maintenance,” he said,
He said that JBPM supports the implementation of regular tree safety audits and assessments, especially in high-risk areas such as main roads, schools, hospitals, public parks, residential areas, and locations with high foot traffic.
Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad said that emergency calls related to fallen trees remain consistently high, ranging between 4,400 and 5,200 cases per year, while for the first half of 2026 alone, 1,912 cases were recorded.— Picture via Facebook
“The audit needs to be conducted by the local authorities (PBTs), the premises owner, or the responsible agency, involving qualified officers or experts. The inspection should include the condition of the trunk, branches, canopy, root system, tilt level, signs of decay, diseases, and the impact of development work around the tree,” he said.
“Trees that have been identified as high-risk need to be acted upon immediately, such as pruning, treatment, support installation, or controlled felling if they pose a threat to public safety.
“JBPM believes that regular audits allow early signs of tree structure failure to be identified before incidents occur, thereby reducing the risk of injury, loss of life, property damage, and disruption to public pathways,” he said.
He said that although the management and maintenance of trees fall under the jurisdiction of the relevant parties, the JBPM is ready to cooperate in terms of sharing incident information, identifying locations where incidents frequently occur, and coordinating preparedness for adverse weather conditions.
In an effort to strengthen prevention, Nor Hisham suggested that the sharing of data on fallen tree incident locations recorded by JBPM be fully utilised by local authorities to identify areas where incidents frequently recur.
“Other collaborations that can be strengthened include mapping high-risk areas, joint inspections, coordinating actions before the monsoon season or periods of bad weather, and faster reporting channels,” he said.
Commenting on operational readiness, Nor Hisham said that JBPM has sufficient personnel, machinery, and equipment to handle fallen tree incidents on a normal and localised scale.
“JBPM also collaborates with local authorities, the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), the Malaysian Civil Defence Force (APM), utility companies, the Public Works Department (JKR), and related agencies to expedite tree removal, traffic control, and ensure the safety of the incident area,” he also said.
He also advised the public to always be alert to weather forecasts and warnings issued by METMalaysia through the official website, the myCuaca app and official social media channels. — Bernama

Title: Sabah teacher uses Jawi to bridge cultural and religious differences in Beluran
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Aug 15 — For Lorenica Frenila Masundim, teaching Jawi script at a school in Sabah’s interior is more than a lesson in writing, it is a way of bringing students and the wider community closer while fostering understanding across racial, religious and cultural differences.
The 36-year-old teacher at Sekolah Kebangsaan Bawang in Beluran sees Jawi lessons as an opportunity to broaden students’ understanding of the national language’s heritage, particularly among those who initially viewed the script as foreign and linked it exclusively to Islam.
Lorenica said she found great fulfilment in seeing non-Muslim students who were once unfamiliar with Jawi gradually learn to read and understand their function as part of the Malay writing system.
“There were students who used to say Jawi was too difficult, but after using the transliteration technique in the application I created, they were able to read it in a short time. As a teacher, seeing their understanding of Jawi change gives me a satisfaction that is hard to describe,” she told
Bernama.
Her Rungus background and Christian faith have never been an obstacle for Lorenica in learning about Jawi, with her role as a Bahasa Melayu teacher encouraging her to understand the script and its place in the national language.
“Just like the Malay language, I have never seen Jawi as belonging to any particular race or religion. To me, it is a national treasure that all Malaysians should learn and preserve,” she said.
Lorenica was first introduced to the Jawi script in 2009 when she took the Basic Introduction to Jawi Writing course for one semester at the Institute of Teacher Education, Gaya Campus in Kota Kinabalu.
Over the next 15 years, she continued to build her knowledge of Jawi before getting the opportunity to teach the script in 2024 and further develop her teaching approach through PhD research under the Ministry of Education’s Hadiah Latihan Persekutuan (HLP) sponsorship.
To help students master Jawi more easily, she developed the PANtaS baCA Jawi (PASCA-ج) application, combining transliteration techniques, interactive exercises and self-directed learning as part of her PhD research.
Lorenica said learning the language or writing systems of other communities not only broadened knowledge but also fostered respect, empathy and mutual appreciation, while helping to overcome prejudice stemming from a lack of understanding.
“Education is a bridge that brings us together despite our differences,  and I believe cross-cultural learning can strengthen national unity, especially through Jawi, which is one of the writing systems used for our national languag,” she said.
Lorenica’s dedication to encouraging wider appreciation of the Jawi script has earned her several accolades, including the Tokoh Ibnu Uraiqith Maulidur Rasul 2024, IMTIYAZ MURABBI Award: Jawi Cross-Cultural Inspiration Teacher 2025 and Sabah Education Excellence Award 2025.
However, she said the Dewan Bahasa dan Pustaka Ikon Wibawa Jawi 2024 award held a special place in her heart, coming after a 12-second video showcasing her efforts to teach Jawi went viral on social media.
“I received this award when I was just starting to teach Jawi. At that time, I had not contributed much, apart from a 12-second video that went viral, but I took the award as a trust and responsibility, and it motivated me to keep going and achieve what I have today,” she said.
In conjunction with this year’s National Day and Malaysia Day (HKHM) celebrations, Lorenica said harmony in a plural society was about being able to live together despite differences in identity, with understanding and mutual respect.
“Sabah is a good example of how communities of different races and religions can live together in mutual respect. As an educator, I believe unity begins in the classroom, where students learn to accept, understand and respect each other’s cultures.
“That is the true spirit of harmony in diversity,” she said. — Bernama

Title: Sabah leaders’ presence at PKR congress reflects strong ties, cooperation, says Mustapha
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 15 — Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor, who is also Gabungan Rakyat Sabah (GRS) chairman, and other leaders’ attendance at the 2026 PKR National Congress today reflects the strong ties and spirit of cooperation between Sabah and federal governments.
Sabah PKR Leadership Council chairman Datuk Mustapha Sakmud said the cooperation extended beyond politics, encompassing all aspects.
“Our priority is to ensure that stability translates into development, economic opportunities, better basic amenities and solutions to issues that are closely related to the lives of the people of Sabah,” he said in a statement today.
Mustapha, who is also Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Sabah and Sarawak Affairs), said the MADANI Government led by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had a responsibility to ensure that national development was implemented inclusively and equitably, taking into account the needs and unique characteristics of every region, including Sabah.
He added that PKR would also remain consistent in championing Sabah’s rights and interests, including the implementation of the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) within a fair federal framework that respected the state’s position and special status.
Mustapha also expressed deep appreciation for the presence of Hajiji and GRS leaders as special guests.
Among the GRS leaders present were Deputy Chief Minister I Datuk Seri Dr Joachim Gunsalam, Sabah Rural Development Minister Datuk Rubin Balang and Sabah Youth, Sports Development and Creative Economy Minister Datuk Nizam Abu Bakar Titingan.
Also present were Sabah Education, Science and Technology Minister Datuk James Ratib, GRS deputy secretary-general Datuk Mohd Razali Mohd Razi and Balung assemblyman Syed Ahmad Syed Abas.
“Their presence at the PKR National Congress sends a message that political differences should not be a barrier to us sitting together and building mutual understanding when it comes to the interests of Sabah and its people,” Mustapha said.
Anwar, who is also PKR president, today officiated the 2026 PKR National Congress themed ‘Memugar Reformasi, Membina Madani’ at the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC) here. — Bernama

Title: Auditor-general: Audit reports key to strengthening accountability, transparency and governance
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 15 — The National Audit Department (JAN) is carrying out its mandate as the country’s audit institution independently, professionally and with integrity in strengthening accountability, transparency and governance in the public sector, says Auditor General Datuk Seri Wan Suraya Wan Mohd Radzi.
She said audit findings were translated into the Auditor General’s Report (LKAN), which is one of the important instruments in the country’s checks-and-balances mechanism.
She said the Auditor General’s firmness in providing opinions on Financial Statements and making audit recommendations was not merely to fulfil reporting requirements to Parliament, but more importantly, to encourage effective corrective action and improvements in public sector management.
“Through the LKAN, weaknesses and non-compliance can be identified, corrective action can be taken, and systems and governance can be strengthened.
“The ultimate goal is to ensure public funds are managed and spent prudently and transparently, while delivering the appropriate value and benefits to the people,” she said in her speech at the 2026 Auditor General’s Cup Debate Competition (PKAN 2026), themed “120 Years of the National Audit Department: Driving Accountability, Building an Integrity-Driven Madani Generation”.
The inaugural PKAN 2026 brought together 20 public higher education institutions from across the country and was held over three days from Aug 13, with the final round taking place at the Parliament building today.
Meanwhile, Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul said in his speech that the debate competition provided a platform for the younger generation to appreciate the importance of accountability, governance and public funds management, besides understanding the role of JAN in ensuring that the people’s trust is upheld.
He said the competition was not merely a platform for debating skills, but also an important avenue for developing a younger generation capable of managing differences of opinion in an orderly, rational and respectful manner.
“A mature democracy does not depend solely on the strength of arguments, but also on how differences are respected, debates are conducted responsibly and rules are observed,” he said.
He said Malaysia needed a younger generation that was not only excellent academically, but also critical-minded, courageous in leadership and understood the country’s administrative and democratic processes.
Universiti Putra Malaysia (UPM) emerged as the PKAN 2026 champions after defeating the International Islamic University Malaysia (IIUM) in the final round, which debated the motion “This House Believes That a Culture of Accountability Should Complement Punitive Action in Addressing Governance Failures”.
UIAM finished as the runners-up, while Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) and Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) shared third place. — Bernama

Title: On-demand car sharing platform, Socar is shutting down in Malaysia after 8 years of operations.
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 15 — Users have recently received messages and notification in the app, informing that the service will end on 31st August 2026.
If you have remaining Wallet balance with the platform, you are able to request for a full refund.
Effective today, the Socar app will no longer accept Wallet top-ups and new monthly pass subscriptions. If you have an existing subscription, they will be issuing refunds on a prorated basis.
However, take note that only Socar will cease operations as its peer-to-peer service, Trevo, is still available in Malaysia.
Unlike Socar which essentially works like an on-demand car rental service, Trevo is essentially an “Airbnb” of sorts for car sharing. This is where vehicle owners (the host) can rent out their rides for weekend and holiday trips and earn money for sharing their vehicle.
Socar was officially launched in 2018 and unlike a typical car rental service, Socar deploys a fleet of vehicles across various hotspots including condominium carparks, shopping malls, transportation hubs and hotels, to make it easier for commuters to get a ride when they need to.
The best part is users can rent by the hour and everything is managed from the app including vehicle inspection, unlocking the vehicle and returning the vehicle. It was seen as a potential disruptor to car ownership as it fills a gap to complement eHailing and public transport. With the end of Socar in Malaysia, the next closest alternative is Gocar.
At the time of writing, Socar is still operational in South Korea and they have Koro that’s catered to foreign drivers.
A little over a week before Socar announced the end of its Malaysian car-sharing service, South Korea’s SK Inc, which is the largest shareholder of Socar Mobility Malaysia, was reported to be buying out the entire stake held by its financial investors.
According to Korea Economic Daily, the deal would allow the investors to exit after SocarMobility Malaysia’s planned initial public offering (IPO) did not materialise. The transaction reportedly involves a USD6 million (about RM25 million) debt swap.
SK Inc entered Malaysia’s mobility market in 2017 through a joint venture with South Korea’s Socar and subsequently secured management rights in Socar Mobility Malaysia in 2020. In 2021, private equity firm EastBridge Partners and Sime Darby Berhad invested a combined KRW65 billion in the company, which at the time was valued at around KRW250 billion.
In 2023, SK said Socar Malaysia had 1.9 million members and commanded over 90% of Malaysia’s car-sharing market. —
SoyaCincau

Title: Fahmi: PKR to strengthen communication strategy to better convey govt messages
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 16 — Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) will strengthen its communication strategy, particularly in information dissemination, to ensure the government’s messages are conveyed more clearly to the public.
PKR Information Chief, who is also Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil, said the move followed several proposals raised by delegates at the ongoing PKR National Congress 2026 at the Melaka International Trade and Exhibition Centre (MITC), Ayer Keroh.
“This is important (to strengthen information dissemination and communication). Many have said that despite various government efforts and achievements, especially those related to macroeconomic matters, these have yet to be translated into improvements felt at the household level.
“This is among the key messages for me, the Communications Ministry, as well as in my capacity as Information Chief and Communications Director of Pakatan Harapan,” he told reporters after visiting the media room during the congress here today.
Fahmi said several views and planned changes related to information dissemination and communication proposals would be presented during the winding-up session tomorrow.
“I remain open to these views and appreciate the willingness of branch leaders who have expressed their commitment to play a greater role in disseminating information.
“Such a channel has existed before, but perhaps a more formal arrangement is needed to ensure issues at the parliamentary level can be brought to our attention in Putrajaya and solutions can be worked out,” he said.
Fahmi said the party’s Central Leadership Council (MPP) was receptive to all proposals raised by delegates and would lead the transformation by making changes within the party’s own leadership first. — Bernama

Title: PKR Selangor delegate calls for party to use own logo in Melaka polls
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 15 — A Selangor PKR delegate today proposed that the party return to using its own logo in future elections, starting with the upcoming Melaka state election.
Ahmad Danish Hairudin, who is also PKR national Youth information chief, said it was timely for the party to campaign under its own logo in the state polls.
He reminded party members that the PKR logo had once represented the Malaysian voice in toppling the arrogance of Umno and the Barisan Nasional (BN) coalition for the first time in the watershed 2018 general election.
“The time has come for Keadilan to use its own logo in the upcoming elections. We start in Melaka, which will face the state election soon,” he said when debating the presidential policy address at the PKR national congress at the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC) here today.
PKR has used its iconic blue-and-white logo in several elections.
Most notably, the party’s logo was used by the newly formed Pakatan Harapan (PH) coalition in the 14th general election (GE14) in 2018, as PH’s red arrowhead logo had not yet been officially registered with the Registrar of Societies (RoS).
That same year, PKR also used its own logo in the Sungai Kandis by-election in Selangor.
In the 2020 Sabah state election, PKR also contested under its own logo, while other PH component parties used the coalition’s logo.
Meanwhile, Ahmad Danish urged PKR not to compromise too much in its political cooperation with Umno to the point of sacrificing the party’s dignity and interests.
He called on the party to instead chart its own political future.
Ahmad Danish cited PKR’s experience in the recent Johor and Negeri Sembilan state elections as lessons for the party leadership.
“In Johor, we were back stabbed by Umno. In Negeri Sembilan, we were decapitated by Umno while we were living in the same house.
“So, do we still want to remain silent?” he said.
Ahmad Danish said the grassroots wanted a clear political decision from PKR president Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and the party leadership on the party’s direction.
He said the leadership should not be too focused on looking after the interests of other parties at the expense of its own members and grassroots.
“Today, the grassroots no longer want the political relationship with Umno-BN, but request that the party’s leadership make a decision to enable the party to move forward,” he said to applause.
The PKR congress comes as the party grapples with the departure of high-profile leaders, resignations of MPs and dismal showings in the recent Negeri Sembilan and Johor state elections.
These developments have also contributed to low morale and growing internal dissent within PKR.

Title: Subang airport runway reopens after helicopter explosion, eight flights diverted
Article:
SUBANG, Aug 15 — The runway at Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah Airport here has been reopened after being temporarily closed following a helicopter exploding and catching fire during an engine run-up test earlier this afternoon.
Malaysian Civil Aviation Authority (CAAM) chief executive officer Capt Datuk Norazman Mahmud said the incident occurred at Taxiway Victor, leading to a temporary suspension of flights.
“The runway was reopened for air traffic at 2.57pm. Passengers are advised to check with their respective airlines for the latest updates on their flights,” he said when contacted today.
Norazman said during the runway closure, eight inbound flights were diverted to other airports, while three departing flights had to be delayed.
Meanwhile, flight information displays at the airport showed revised schedules for several flights to various destinations.
Earlier, CAAM had announced that the runway was temporarily closed, with all departures and arrivals suspended until further notice.
The explosion involving a Kamov KaV-32S helicopter owned by a Ukraine-registered company occurred at 12.28pm. The aircraft caught fire during a ground engine run-up test as part of maintenance activities.
Four Ukrainian men comprising the pilot, co-pilot, and two crew members were conducting the maintenance. One of them suffered minor injuries from flying debris. — Bernama

Title: Not our facility, not our customer: Aviation company distances itself from Subang helicopter fire
Article:
SUBANG JAYA, Aug 15 — An aviation maintenance company today denied any connection to the Kamov Ka-32 helicopter that caught fire at Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah Airport here, saying the aircraft was not its customer and the incident did not occur at its facility.
The clarification by KarbonMRO came after the Selangor Fire and Rescue Department said the helicopter caught fire during an engine test following maintenance work at the airport, with four people escaping, one who was injured by debris.
“The incident did not take place at KarbonMRO’s facility, and the helicopter involved is not a KarbonMRO customer,” the company’s head of marketing Trixie Guantero was quoted by news outlet
Free Malaysia Today
as saying in a statement.
Guantero said safety, accuracy and professional integrity were fundamental to the company’s operations.
The Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) said the incident occurred at Taxiway Victor, temporarily disrupting airport operations before the runway reopened at 2.57pm.
CAAM chief executive officer Norazman Mahmud said eight inbound flights were diverted to other airports while three departing flights were delayed during the temporary closure.
The Selangor Fire and Rescue Department earlier said it received an emergency call at 12.30pm and found the helicopter fully engulfed in flames when firefighters arrived.
The aircraft, registered UR-CIT in Ukraine, had four Ukrainians on board who managed to escape, while one person outside the helicopter was reported to have been struck by debris.
The circumstances surrounding the incident remain under investigation.

Title: No Malaysians reported affected by earthquake in Indonesia’s Flores, says embassy
Article:
JAKARTA, Aug 15 — No Malaysians have been reported affected by the magnitude 7.7 earthquake that struck Flores in Indonesia’s East Nusa Tenggara (NTT) province early today.
The Malaysian Embassy in Jakarta said it had contacted Malaysians in NTT who were registered with the embassy, as well as Malaysian tourists who had informed the embassy of their whereabouts in the region.
“The Embassy is also in close contact with the Indonesian Ministry of Foreign Affairs to obtain the latest situation update and, as of noon local time, there have been no reports of incidents involving Malaysian nationals,” the embassy said in a statement.
Malaysians affected by the earthquake and requiring consular assistance can contact the Malaysian Embassy in Jakarta via +62 813 8081 3036 or email mwjakarta@kln.gov.my.
The embassy also expressed its sympathy to those affected and hoped that the authorities’ efforts to manage the situation on the ground would proceed smoothly.
The earthquake struck at 4.58am local time, with its epicentre in the sea about 30 kilometres (km) from Mbay at a depth of 15 km. It also triggered a tsunami warning, which the Meteorology, Climatology and Geophysics Agency (BMKG) lifted at 7.31am after monitoring showed no further significant rise in sea levels.
The National Disaster Management Agency (BNPB) said about 2,000 residents had been evacuated or had fled to safety following the earthquake that struck Flores Island.
Earlier, the Maumere Search and Rescue Office reported that the death toll from the earthquake and several strong aftershocks had risen to 20, with six people injured and two others still trapped. — Bernama

Title: Myanmar refugee, two young sons die in Bagan Serai house fire
Article:
IPOH, Aug 15 — Three Myanmar refugees comprising a man and his two sons, died while his wife was injured in a house fire in Taman Serai Maju, Bagan Serai, early this morning.
Perak Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) director Datuk Sayani Saidon said the deceased victims were identified as Mohd Yunus Nor Ali, 27, Muhammad Woheed Mohd Yunus, 6, and Mohamad Aheed Mohd Yunus, 3, while the victim’s wife, Saniya Jahan Juma Abul Kasim, 24, who is also a Myanmar refugee, suffered burns on her hands and feet.
“The Perak JBPM received an emergency call through the MERS 999 line at 5.17am before the first vehicle arrived at the scene at 5.30am. When the team arrived, a Class A house measuring 20 feet x 40 feet, inhabited by seven foreign nationals, was on fire with damage estimated at around 70 per cent.
“The victim’s wife, who was found outside the house, said her husband and two children were still trapped inside the premises,” he said in a statement.
Sayani said that upon arriving at the location, his team immediately conducted a search and rescue operation using the RECEO concept before three victims were found in the first room that was on fire.
He said the medical officers from the Ministry of Health (MOH) who arrived at the scene confirmed that all three victims had died, while the injured woman was given initial treatment before being sent to hospital using the Emergency Medical Rescue Services (EMRS) vehicle.
He also said that the deceased victims had been handed over to the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) for further action, and that the fire was brought under control at 6.20am, with the operation fully completed by 7.35am.
“A thorough investigation is being conducted at the scene to identify the actual cause of the fire and to estimate the losses.
“Based on the information and initial findings by the JBPM forensic team, the fire started in the first room, which is where the victims were found burned. The cause of the fire and the extent of the damage are still under investigation,” he added. — Bernama

Title: ‘Beginning, not the end’: Abim calls for broader higher education reform after AUKU repeal
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 15 — The repeal of the Universities and University Colleges Act (AUKU) 1971 will create new opportunities to reform the country’s higher education framework, said the Muslim Youth Movement of Malaysia (Abim).
Welcoming the move to repeal the Act, Abim president Ahmad Fahmi Mohd Samsudin called on the government to formulate a comprehensive post-AUKU legal framework covering the country’s entire higher education ecosystem.
He said the focus should now be on building a new higher education ecosystem that strikes a balance between student freedom and strong institutional governance.
“The repeal of AUKU does not remove the need for strong university governance. The post-AUKU framework must strike a balance between student and academic freedom and institutional autonomy, integrity, accountability and academic excellence.
“This reform must go beyond activism and be felt by all students through more meaningful involvement in matters affecting education, welfare and campus life,” he said in a statement today.
Ahmad Fahmi said the legal changes must be accompanied by efforts to foster a campus culture that encourages students to think, exchange views, engage in organisations and contribute to society.
He also called for the principles of academic freedom and students’ rights to be given due consideration across the education system, including in reviewing the suitability of amendments to the Private Higher Educational Institutions Act 1996 (Act 555) and the Universiti Teknologi MARA Act 1976 (Act 173).
Therefore, he said the development of a post-AUKU framework must involve comprehensive engagement with students, academics, university administrators and relevant stakeholders.
“For Abim, freedom must go hand in hand with good manners, integrity in the pursuit of knowledge and mas’uliyyah (responsibility). The challenge after AUKU is not only to provide greater space for students, but to nurture a generation that can fill it with knowledge, intellectual courage, maturity and responsibility.
“The repeal of AUKU should mark the beginning, not the end, of higher education reform,” he said.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said earlier today that the government would repeal AUKU to provide greater freedom and democratic space for the student movement in the country, with the proposal to be tabled before the Cabinet next Wednesday. — Bernama

Title: As PKR grapples with departures, Anwar makes fresh appeal for estranged old friends to return
Article:
AYER KEROH, Aug 15 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today appealed to former PKR leaders and members who have drifted away from the party to return, while apologising to those who may have felt sidelined.
His call comes as PKR faces a series of internal tensions and recent departures, including former Subang MP Wong Chen who quit the party earlier this week, while former leaders Chua Tian Chang and Dr Xavier Jayakumar were seen at the party’s national congress here today.
“
Otai-otai.
.. please return,” Anwar was quoted by news portal
Malaysiakini
as saying in his policy speech at the PKR National Congress 2026 at the Melaka International Trade Centre here.
Otai-otai
is Malay slang for ‘old hands’ or veterans.
“For my other friends, who may have felt a little marginalised – if we have made any mistakes, I apologise. Return to the path of our struggle,” Anwar added.
Anwar’s appeal for reconciliation comes ahead of the next general election, with PKR also facing questions over its electoral performance following setbacks in Johor, Sabah and Negeri Sembilan.
Earlier today, PKR Women’s information chief Ginie Lim posted a photograph of herself with Chua, better known as Tian Chua, and Dr Xavier at the congress, marking a notable reunion of former party figures.
Chua was sacked from PKR after contesting the Batu parliamentary seat as an independent in the last general election, while Dr Xavier resigned from the party in 2021 after supporting then-prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin.
Wong, who served PKR for 17 years, resigned from the party on August 10 and joined Bersama, which is co-led by former PKR leaders Rafizi Ramli and Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad.
PKR is also dealing with uncertainty over its deputy presidency after Anwar’s daughter Nurul Izzah Anwar sought to resign from the post, with the party instead placing her on indefinite temporary leave and assigning her duties to vice-president Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
Nurul Izzah has since reiterated her intention to step down, saying she plans to pursue further studies and focus on commitments outside politics.
In Negeri Sembilan, PKR retained only two of the five state seats it previously held despite contesting 16 constituencies, including former menteri besar Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun, who lost his seat.
Six PKR state division chiefs subsequently wrote to Anwar seeking a review of Aminuddin’s leadership following the result.
The party’s recent setbacks and departures have added pressure on Anwar to strengthen internal cohesion as PKR prepares for the next electoral contest.

Title: Motac cracks down on unlicensed tourism operators in KL, issues 15 notices
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 15 — The Ministry of Tourism, Arts and Culture (Motac) issued 15 inspection notices for various offences under the Tourism Industry Act 1992 (Act 482) during a two-day enforcement operation that began on Wednesday around Kuala Lumpur.
In a statement today, Motac said nine of the notices were issued under Subsection 5(2) for operating a tourism business without a valid licence.
“Three tourist locations, nine business premises and three individuals were inspected over the course of the operation.
“Intelligence work in collaboration with the Kuala Lumpur Tourist Guide Association (KLTGA) was also carried out to detect individuals suspected of carrying out tourist guide activities without valid licences. Enforcement action under Subsection 21(1) was taken against those found doing so,” the statement read.
The ministry said the operation also flagged other violations, including using private or unlicensed vehicles to ferry tourists, breaching licence conditions and doing business with unlicensed operators.
Private or unlicensed vehicles used for tourist transport that have been identified will be dealt with by the Land Public Transport Agency and Road Transport Department.
“Further investigations will be conducted before legal action is taken against individuals, entities, owners and other relevant parties involved,” the statement read.
Motac warned unlicensed parties not to offer tourism services, adding that offences under Act 482 are liable for compounds of up to RM250,000 or a fine of up to RM500,000, imprisonment of up to 10 years, or both, upon conviction.
“Motac remains committed to enforcing the law thoroughly, firmly and effectively, guided by the principles of good governance, fairness, integrity, and accountability, in line with the Malaysia Madani vision.
“The public and industry players are encouraged to channel any information on tourism activities suspected of violating laws and regulations through the Public Complaints Management System (SISPAA) at the following link: [https://motac.spab.gov.my/eApps/system/index.do,”](https://motac.spab.gov.my/eApps/system/index.do,”) the statement read. — Bernama

Title: Federal govt aims to cut Terengganu poor households to 20,000 by year-end
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU, Aug 15 — The federal government aims to reduce the number of poor households in Terengganu to 20,000 by this December.
Deputy director-general of the Strategic Development, Implementation Coordination Unit (ICU), under the Prime Minister’s Department (ICU JPM), Datuk Norashiken Ishak, said as of August 13, the number of poor households in Terengganu was recorded at 24,100 households, compared to 26,800 households in early July.
“This effort is the result of coordinated actions by the Terengganu ICU JPM together with related agencies that can increase income, expand economic opportunities, and stabilise the lives of eKasih participants,” she said.
She said this to reporters after completing the Program Jelajah Kesejahteraan Rakyat 2026 for the Kuala Terengganu and Kuala Nerus zones, organised by the Terengganu ICU JPM, at the Hiliran People’s Housing Project (PPR) here today.
Norashiken said that additionally, her team has also succeeded in improving the living standards and welfare of the B40, especially eKasih participants, through 310 Rumah Kasih Ihsan projects implemented as of August this year, covering a total allocation of RM18.44 million.
She also said the total includes 161 new construction projects, 146 house renovation projects, and three new stilt house construction projects.
“So, InsyaAllah, we will continue this effort and contribution, and it is also the commitment of the Madani Government to ensure the well-being of the people,” she added.
Meanwhile, the Program Jelajah Kesejahteraan Rakyat 2026 for the Kuala Terengganu and Kuala Nerus zones, held today, brings together the services and interventions from various agencies to facilitate the community, especially the eKasih households, in obtaining assistance and services according to their needs.
Based on the value of Ihsan, the programmr was enlivened by the presence of 4,000 visitors, including 700 eKasih participants, and featured 18 government service booths for advisory services, eligibility checks and assistance matching. — Bernama

Title: Five PKR figures honoured with posthumous awards
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 15 — The contributions and sacrifices of five PKR figures were honoured posthumously at the 2026 PKR National Congress here today.
Four received the Bill Kayong Award, while the fifth was awarded the Dr Syed Husin Ali Pejuang Rakyat Award, introduced for the first time in recognition of the late Syed Husin’s contributions as a PKR founder and advocate of social justice.
The Bill Kayong Award was presented to the late Sapiah Zaini, former Miri Women’s chief; the late Hasbul Syafiqi Hasbullah, Keadilan Penang working secretary; and party activists, the late Syafiq Ali Abdullah@Abang Mani, and the late Muhammad Shahhanaz Nazarudin.
The award, named after the late Sarawak activist Bill Kayong, recognises individuals who have made significant contributions to the party’s struggle and grassroots work.
Syafiq’s older brother, Ahmad Sulaiman Selvarajah Abdullah, said the recognition meant a great deal to his family and strengthened their resolve to continue supporting PKR.
“…we are extremely happy and deeply honoured by this recognition of his immense contribution to Keadilan and the reform movement from the party’s founding in 1998 until today,” he said after accepting the award.
Hasbul Syafiqi’s mother, Normala Ghazali, said her son, better known as Black, had helped many friends in Penang and was known by party members across the country for always being willing to lend a hand.
“This recognition shows that many people still remember and cherish him to this day. To me, Black left this world having made a meaningful contribution to others,” she said.
Former senator Datuk Mustafa Kamal Mohd Yusoff, better known as Pak Mus, received the Dr Syed Husin Ali Pejuang Rakyat Award in recognition of his dedication and contribution to strengthening the party’s electoral machinery and understanding of election operations.
Meanwhile, the Tawau branch in Sabah took first place in the Highest Membership Registration Award, with the Bukit Gantang branch in Perak finishing second and the Indera Mahkota branch in Pahang third.
The number of new Keadilan ranting (sub-branches) rose to 1,354 this year, up from 520 last year, indicating increased grassroots participation among party members.
In the State and National Highest Number of Ranting Competition, Putatan branch in Sabah took first place, followed by Tanah Merah branch in Kelantan in second and Bangi branch in Selangor in third. — Bernama

Title: MOH to reopen four training institutes next year amid critical nurse shortage
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Aug 15 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) is strengthening three key strategies under the country’s health workforce reform to address the critical shortage of nurses, said Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad.
He said the three strategies involved increasing the number of nursing graduates, expanding career pathways and implementing direct recruitment and greater autonomy in staffing management.
“Of the 73,281 Grade U5 nurse positions, there are currently 10,557 vacancies in health facilities,” he said in his speech at the 2026 Ministry of Health Training Institute (ILKKM) Sabah Zone Convocation at the Chancellor’s Hall, Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS), today.
Dzulkefly said the move was important in meeting the country’s health workforce needs amid the increasingly complex challenges facing the health system.
Under the strategy to increase the nursing workforce, he said the intake of nurse trainees had been increased to 3,000 a year from 2025.
“To expand this strategy, the MOH aims to outsource up to 2,000 trainees a year to Public Higher Education Institutions (IPTA) and Private Higher Education Institutions (IPTS),” he said.
In addition, he said four ILKKM branches in Kuantan, Kuala Terengganu, Muar and Penang would reopen by October 2027, providing additional capacity for about 500 trainees.
“This brings the total capacity of the Diploma in Nursing programme to 5,500 trainees a year,” he added.
For the second strategy, Dzulkefly said the MOH would roll out 15 On-the-Job Training (OJT) programmes this September to enable staff to enhance their expertise without having to leave their workplace for long periods.
“The ministry is also expanding the career pathway for community nurses to become nurses through the Transition Diploma,” he said.
Under the third strategy, Dzulkefly said the Public Service Department (JPA) had approved an exemption from Interim Contract Appointments for eligible ILKKM Diploma in Nursing graduates.
“This means that all ILKKM Diploma in Nursing graduates who have successfully completed the programme and are registered with the Nursing Board of Malaysia will be absorbed directly to permanent positions,” he said.
Dzulkefly said that, since July 9, 2026, the ministry had also been granted autonomy in staffing management to reduce bureaucracy and facilitate the direct placement of graduates in the field. — Bernama

Title: Sabah hospital sexual harassment case: MOH moves director out, complainant under treatment, PSD to decide next step
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Aug 15 — The Health Ministry has completed its internal investigation into an alleged sexual harassment case involving a Sabah hospital director and transferred the officer to a medical post at the Sabah Health Department.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad said the ministry had also submitted its report to the Public Service Department (PSD), which has jurisdiction over further action based on the officer’s grade,
The New Straits Times
reported.
“Administratively, the ministry has completed the internal investigation. Among the actions taken was the transfer of the director to a medical officer’s position in the medical division of the Sabah Health Department,” he was quoted as saying at a press conference after the ministry’s Training Institutes convocation at Universiti Malaysia Sabah here today.
Dzulkefly said the alleged victim had been given full support and psychiatric treatment and had since returned to a better working environment.
“The official report from the department has been submitted to Public Service Department, based on the officer’s grade, as it has its own jurisdiction and authority to handle this matter,” he said.
The case was raised publicly last month by Kapayan assemblyman Chin Teck Ming and Sabah Warisan Health Bureau chief Dr Istefan Koh over alleged wrongdoing involving the hospital director.
Sabah police commissioner Datuk Jauteh Dikun had also confirmed that a police report was lodged earlier this year.
Dzulkefly said the ministry had taken administrative action after completing its internal probe, while any further disciplinary action would fall within the PSD’s jurisdiction.

Title: Sabah-based KDM cuts ties with GRS govt, says it’s time to win back grassroots
Article:
KINARUT, Aug 15 — Parti Kesejahteraan Demokratik Masyarakat (KDM) today pulled its support for the Gabungan Rakyat Sabah (GRS)-led state government, signalling a shift in the party’s political direction ahead of the next general election.
KDM acting president Priscella Peter said the decision was made by the party’s supreme council during its annual meeting today, local media reported.
“What is important is that, in preparation for the next general election, KDM, together with its supreme council, has decided to move forward without being part of the GRS government,” she was quoted by news outlet Free Malaysia Today as saying at press conference in Papar.
She said the decision, which was not made lightly, was intended to make KDM’s position clear to the public and its grassroots supporters.
Priscella said the party had been affected by what happened after the previous state election, prompting it to make its position known well before the next polls.
“What happened after the last state election has certainly had an impact on our grassroots,” she said.
She said KDM wanted to show that its political decisions were not driven solely by the timing of elections, but reflected a longer-term commitment to its supporters.
“We need to take action beforehand to demonstrate our commitment and regain the trust of our grassroots,” she said.
The move comes a week after Warisan president Datuk Seri Shafie Apdal said his party was in discussions with KDM and Parti Solidariti Tanah Airku over a possible cooperation for the 16th general election.
Shafie said no agreement had been reached, but any pact involving Warisan would safeguard Sabah’s rights and interests.
KDM contested the November 2025 state election independently and won one seat, Paginatan, before subsequently aligning itself with the GRS administration led by Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor.

Title: Onn Hafiz: Bangsa Johor rental deposit aid of RM1,000 to roll out next year
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 15 — The Johor government is expected to introduce the RM1,000 Bangsa Johor rental deposit assistance next year to help people in the state who face difficulties coming up with the upfront payment for accommodation.
Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi said the initiative, implemented through the Johor State Housing Development Corporation (PKPJ), is being introduced in response to complaints from tenants who face difficulties paying the upfront amount or rental deposit.
He said applications for the initiative would also be open to federal civil servants serving in Johor, such as teachers, nurses, medical officers, police personnel and members of the armed forces.
“Apart from rental assistance, there have been calls for the government to consider rental deposit assistance, especially for those who have just started working... perhaps many of them cannot afford it yet.
“We want to expand this assistance so that it benefits not only Bangsa Johor but also those who have recently moved to Johor, particularly federal civil servants. They serve in Johor, are part of Bangsa Johor and are working for us,” he said.
He said this at a press conference after the Phase 5 of the Perumahan Kasih Johor Initiative ceremony at the Larkin Indoor Arena Stadium here today.
Onn Hafiz said the first phase of the rental deposit assistance would target about 10,000 recipients.
Eligible recipients would also be entitled to Rental Assistance of RM2,500, bringing the total assistance available to RM3,500 per person. Eligibility covers individuals residing and working in the state.
He said further details, as well as new housing products, would be announced during the tabling of the Johor Budget in November.
At today’s ceremony, RM22 million was allocated for Phase 5, covering 6,000 recipients of various housing assistance schemes, while Phase 6, scheduled for next month, is expected to benefit another 5,000 recipients.
Overall, the Johor government has spent RM337 million on its housing agenda since 2022, benefiting nearly 100,000 recipients statewide. — Bernama

Title: DoE detects seven hotspots in East Malaysia as transboundary haze worsens air quality
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 15 — A total of seven hotspots were detected in the country, with five in Sarawak and two in Sabah, as air quality deteriorates in several areas of Sarawak, which are currently recording Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at unhealthy levels.
Department of Environment (DOE) deputy director-general (Development) Azuri Azizah Saedon said that, based on the Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC) report dated August 14, a total of 226 hotspots were also detected in Kalimantan, while another five were recorded in Sumatra.
As of 11am today, nine areas in Sarawak recorded unhealthy API readings, with Kuching recording the highest at 164, followed by Samarahan (161), Serian IPD (160), Bintulu and Sarikei (157), Sri Aman (153), Sibu (152), Mukah (151) and Samalaju (118).
“The deterioration in air quality was caused by the movement of haze from various directions, including moderate to dense transboundary smoke plumes from clusters of hotspots in West Kalimantan moving northwards into the western part of the state.
“Moderate to dense localised smoke plumes were also observed, originating from hotspots in large parts of Kalimantan, central Sarawak and central Sumatra,” she said in a statement today.
She said several air quality monitoring stations in West Kalimantan as well as western and central Sarawak also recorded unhealthy readings.
However, ASMC said the full extent of the hotspot and haze situation in the region could not be determined due to cloud cover.
In view of the situation, Azuri Azizah said the DOE had stepped up enforcement action and daily patrols in areas prone to open burning, in addition to monitoring API readings from time to time.
“The National Open Burning Action Plan and National Haze Action Plan have also been activated to coordinate the actions of government agencies in addressing open burning and haze situations,” she said.
She advised landowners to monitor areas that are prone to and frequently affected by fires, including landfill sites, forests, peatlands, plantations, agricultural and industrial areas, and to take measures to prevent intrusion by irresponsible parties.
The public was also reminded not to carry out open burning and to report any cases of open burning or fires to the Fire and Rescue Department at 999 or the DOE’s toll-free line at 1-800-88-2727. — Bernama

Title: If you’re naughty, we will know it, mayor warns as Kota Kinabalu adds 1,600 CCTV cameras to catch vandals
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Aug 15 — A total of 1,600 closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras will be installed across the city soon as City Hall (DBKK) moves to strengthen surveillance and protect public assets from vandalism.
Mayor Datuk Seri Dr Sabin Samitah said funding for the project had been secured, with installation expected to begin soon.
“The expanded surveillance would also help safeguard public assets such as the newly unveiled ‘Remembering Australia Place’ mural from vandalism,” he said during the launch of the mural, Friday.
The project commemorates the historical links between Australia and Sabah, including the contribution of Australian personnel to the rebuilding of Jesselton after the Second World War, while Sabin hoped the artwork would become a vibrant and meaningful heritage destination for Kota Kinabalu.
The “Remembering Australia Place” mural, located on the Wisma Intiutama building in central Kota Kinabalu, was produced by local community arts organisation Pillars of Sabah, with support from the Australian High Commission and involvement from teachers and students of SMK Sanzac.
The mural is intended to tell the story of Australia-Sabah friendship, remembrance and people-to-people ties, with a QR code also planned on site to provide visitors with additional information about the area’s historical significance.
Sabin also said the Kota Kinabalu International Mayors’ Dialogue 2026 would bring together mayors, city leaders, policymakers, development partners and other stakeholders to exchange ideas and practical experiences on the challenges and opportunities facing cities.
He said the dialogue, scheduled for October, reflected Kota Kinabalu’s aspiration to strengthen city-to-city diplomacy and international cooperation, particularly in sustainable and resilient cities, smart city development, climate action, tourism, urban liveability and inclusive economic growth.
In this regard, Sabin invited Australian High Commission representatives and Australian city leaders to support and participate in the international dialogue, noting that two mayors from the United States had confirmed their participation.
He said Australian participation would provide an opportunity to strengthen practical cooperation and relationships between Kota Kinabalu and Australian cities, and expressed hope that the Australian High Commission could help facilitate the attendance of Australian city leaders.
Kota Kinabalu MP and Deputy Minister of Agriculture and Food Security Datuk Chan Foong Hin hoped the mural would help stimulate the arrival of more Australian tourists to Sabah, particularly by strengthening awareness of the historical and contemporary connections between the two sides.
He also welcomed calls to restore direct flights between Australia and Sabah, saying he would raise the matter with his party secretary-general, who is also the Transport Minister. — Daily Express

Title: Threat ends as Sabah wildlife officers kill 14-foot croc near in Sipitang river near jetty to Labuan
Article:
SIPITANG, August 15 — A 14-foot male crocodile was caught and shot dead by the Sabah Wildlife Department (JHL) on Thursday, bringing relief to residents who had been living in fear of the reptile at Kampung Tanjung Pagar.
A village resident said they were grateful for the department’s swift action in dealing with the crocodile, which had earlier been caught using a fishing line.
The crocodile was frequently spotted at the mouth of the river near Kg Tanjung Pagar before it was shot dead and handed over to a licensed crocodile hunter.
However, residents have been warned to remain cautious as other crocodiles could still be in the area.
“There could still be other crocodiles there, so residents need to be careful when they are near the river, as crocodiles can attack suddenly and prey on those who are unaware,” the resident said.
The area is also near the boat jetty serving passengers travelling to Labuan, who have been urged to exercise caution when boarding passenger boats.
The residents thanked the Wildlife Department for successfully capturing and eliminating the crocodile and hoped operations would continue to deal with other crocodiles that could pose a threat to residents and boat passengers.
Meanwhile, villagers at Kg Pelakat Skim, together with the Wildlife Department, have been setting fishing lines in a drain after crocodiles were spotted there.
According to residents, a crocodile had frequently been seen swimming in the drain, raising concerns over the potential danger, particularly to children who often spend time near the area, including those who enjoy fishing.
“We advise residents to be more careful when approaching or playing near the drain,” they said.
The residents said they had lodged a complaint with the Wildlife Department regarding the crocodile, prompting officers to visit the area and set fishing lines in an effort to catch it. — Daily Express

Title: Finance Ministry to roll out RM1.2b in STR cash aid for 5.3 million recipients from today
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 15 — The Ministry of Finance (MOF) said Phase 3 payments of the Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) cash aid will be disbursed in stages starting today to 5.3 million recipients, with an allocation of RM1.2 billion.
The number of recipients has grown by 300,000 since the start of the year, when it stood at five million. Of these, 3.9 million are low- and middle-income households, and 1.4 million are single senior citizens.
“The Phase 3 payments range from RM150 to RM600, depending on income and number of children, while single senior citizens will receive RM150.
“Overall, the total disbursement for the first three phases of 2026 has reached RM3.6 billion,” MOF said in a statement today.
The ministry said, depending on the category they fall under, recipients can collect up to RM3,300 in total by August 2026, combining STR Phases 1 to 3 and the monthly SARA basic aid. This amount does not include the one-off SARA payment for all Malaysian citizens aged 18 and above.
Starting this year, the assistance has been revamped to provide more regular support. STR is paid out quarterly, while SARA delivers monthly basic aid to those who qualify.
In the same statement, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government will continue to ensure that assistance reaches those in need, as the cost of living remains a challenge.
“With the cost of living still posing difficulties for some, the government will continue to ensure that aid reaches those who need it.
“That is why the number of households receiving STR has increased from 3.7 million at the start of the year to 3.9 million for Phase 3.
“STR and SARA help ease the daily needs of Malaysians, while the government continues to implement reforms and strengthen the economy to raise incomes and living standards. Our goal is not just to provide aid, but to ensure that people’s lives improve,” he said.
Meanwhile, MOF said the restructuring of government finances and improvements in governance have enabled more state revenue to be channeled to those in need.
Total allocation for STR and SARA in 2026 amounts to RM15 billion, the highest in the Federal government’s history and nearly three times higher than the Bantuan Rakyat 1Malaysia (BR1M) payments in 2016.
Recipients with bank accounts will receive their Phase 3 STR payments via direct credit starting today. For those without bank accounts, payments can be collected in cash at any Bank Simpanan Nasional branch nationwide.
To minimise leakage, new applications and appeals for STR remain open throughout the year via the official STR portal at bantuantunai.hasil.gov.my.
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) on STR are also available on the portal, while SARA FAQs can be found at sara.gov.my.
MOF also advised the public to remain vigilant against fake links and scams, and to refer only to the official STR portal for the latest information. — Bernama

Title: He saw the crash online and knew something was wrong: Father loses wife, son in Temerloh crash
Article:
TEMERLOH, Aug 15 — A routine wait for his wife’s arrival turned into a frantic search for answers after Saifulnizam Sulaiman realised she had not responded to his messages or calls for hours.
Saifulnizam, 39, was in Seremban for work while his wife, Nur Fatima Syuhada Abdullah, 39, and their 12-year-old son, Muhammad Fattah Aisy Naufal Saifulnizam, were travelling from Jerantut to join him during the school holidays.
“I sent her a message at about 5pm, but there was no reply, and after finishing work at about 7pm, I saw that the message was still unread and my calls were also unanswered,” he told Berita Harian when met at the forensic unit of Sultan Haji Ahmad Shah Hospital here today.
He said his wife would normally keep him updated on their location and journey, and had never failed to answer his messages or calls during their 14 years of marriage.
“That’s why when the message was not read for several hours, I felt that something bad had happened,” he said.
His worst fears grew after he came across social media posts about a crash along Jalan Temerloh-Triang.
“It was then that I saw the accident on Jalan Temerloh-Triang on social media, and the first thing that came to my mind was, ‘That’s my wife and son,’” he said.
Saifulnizam said he contacted relatives in Temerloh to try to reach his wife, but they were also unable to get through to her.
He then drove from Seremban to Temerloh to find out what had happened.
Nur Fatima and Muhammad Fattah were killed after the car they were travelling in collided with a diesel tanker at about 4.30pm yesterday at Kilometre 9 of Jalan Temerloh-Triang.
Both vehicles caught fire following the collision.
Saifulnizam said his wife and son had left Jerantut at about 2pm and were heading to Seremban to help him with his business during the school holidays.
The tanker was carrying 32,000 litres of diesel and was believed to have skidded before colliding with the car.
Videos of the crash circulated on social media, showing both vehicles engulfed in flames shortly after the collision.

Title: New ‘One Higher Education Act’, launched in January, to replace UUCA, Zambry confirms
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 15 — A more comprehensive national higher education legislative framework to replace the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (UUCA) has been outlined under the Malaysia Higher Education Plan (RPTM) 2026-2035, said Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir.
He said the effort was part of the agenda for establishing the One Higher Education Act, which was launched in January 2026.
Zambry said the Higher Education Ministry was taking into account the need to reform the national higher education legislative framework by drafting a new, more comprehensive act to replace UUCA.
“I take note of the Prime Minister’s announcement on the repeal of UUCA during his presidential policy speech at the 2026 PKR National Congress,” he said in a statement today.
Zambry said UUCA was more than legislation governing student affairs and freedom, as it provided the basis for the establishment, administration and governance of universities and university colleges.
“Therefore, its repeal must be accompanied by a new legal framework that is more comprehensive, progressive and aligned with the current and future needs of higher education,” he said.
He said the process would be carried out in an inclusive and comprehensive manner, taking into account the views of all stakeholders, including university leaders, academics, public and private higher education institutions, industry players, polytechnics, community colleges, TVET providers, legal experts and students.
According to Zambry, the move was aimed not just at repealing UUCA, but at establishing a more comprehensive and forward-looking higher education legislative framework that would strengthen institutional autonomy, academic freedom and student voice, while preserving governance, accountability and excellence across higher education institutions.
He said the move was part of the higher education transformation under the RPTM 2026-2035 aimed at ensuring Malaysia’s higher education system remains relevant and dynamic amid changes in the global education landscape.
Earlier, Anwar said the government would repeal UUCA to provide greater freedom and democratic space for the student movement in the country.
He said the move followed a memorandum and views presented by student leaders calling for comprehensive changes to the Act. — Bernama

Title: Helicopter catches fire during engine test at Subang airport, four escape but one hit by debris
Article:
SUBANG JAYA, Aug 15 — A Kamov Ka-32 helicopter caught fire during an engine test at Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah Airport here today, with four people escaping and one person reportedly injured after being struck by debris outside the aircraft.
The Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) confirmed the incident in an X post, saying the runway was closed following the incident and further updates would be issued.
“The fire occurred as the helicopter was about to take off for the purpose of engine testing after repairs,” Selangor Fire and Rescue Department assistant director of operations Ashrul Riezal Asbar said in a statement today.
He said firefighters found the helicopter, registered as UR-CIT in Ukraine, fully engulfed in flames when they arrived after receiving an emergency call at 12.30pm.
The four people on board managed to escape from the helicopter during the fire.
One other person, who was outside the aircraft, was reportedly injured after being struck by debris from the helicopter.
The airport’s Aircraft Rescue and Fire Fighting Service team also assisted in the firefighting operation.
Five firefighters from the Bukit Jelutong Fire and Rescue Station were deployed with a Fire Rescue Tender to the scene.
The circumstances surrounding the incident are still being investigated.

Title: MoH: No significant rise in haze-related illnesses yet
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 15 — Malaysia has not recorded a significant increase in haze-related illnesses so far, but the Ministry of Health (MOH) does not rule out a rise in cases if air quality worsens or the haze persists.
The MOH said no increase had been recorded so far in the three types of haze-related illnesses, namely upper respiratory tract infections (URTI), asthma and conjunctivitis, monitored through sentinel health facilities.
“Monitoring so far has found no significant increase in cases in any state compared with the situation before the haze,” the minisry told Bernama.
In Sarawak, the MOH said monitoring at 12 sentinel health clinics recorded a decline in URTI cases, from 1,473 in Epidemiological Week (EW) 31, before the haze, to 1,347 in EW 32.
Asthma cases fell from 195 to 122, while conjunctivitis cases rose from 15 to 43.
According to the MOH, children, the elderly and those with chronic illnesses are at greater risk of being affected by haze.
It said children have a higher respiratory rate, resulting in greater exposure to haze particles and potential health effects, while they are also less able to make appropriate decisions, particularly in dangerous situations.
Haze can have adverse effects on chronic conditions such as asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and heart disease.
The ministry further said that fine particles in haze can penetrate deep into the lungs, triggering inflammation and shortness of breath, while increasing the risk of heart attacks, acute attacks and hospitalisation.
“Therefore, people with chronic diseases should avoid exposure to haze to prevent their conditions from worsening. They should also follow their doctors’ advice and take their medication regularly,” it said.
The MOH anticipates an increase in haze-related illnesses if the haze persists or air quality worsens, with all health facilities instructed to remain on alert.
The ministry also said it is monitoring haze-related illnesses at health facilities located near the Department of Environment’s air quality monitoring stations.
A total of 68 health facilities have been selected to monitor haze-related illnesses, with data collection increased from weekly before the haze to daily during the haze.
The MOH said that so far, there had been no significant increase in hospital admissions or emergency cases linked to the haze.
However, the ministry said it would continue monitoring the situation and take appropriate action to treat patients with haze-related illnesses.
Meanwhile, the MOH advised the public to avoid outdoor physical activities to reduce exposure to haze, as increased breathing rates during physical activity can result in more suspended particles entering the respiratory tract.
“The public is also advised to stay indoors as much as possible and, if they need to go outside, limit their time outdoors and use appropriate face masks.
“Windows should also be kept closed to reduce haze entering homes or buildings,” it said, urging the public to avoid smoking and other activities that could increase indoor air pollution, and to keep their surroundings clean.
When driving, the public is also advised to use air conditioning in recirculation mode and drink plenty of plain water, with at least eight glasses a day recommended to stay hydrated.
The MOH said indoor air quality can also be improved by using air conditioning and high-efficiency air filters or purifiers to remove fine particles and prevent the entry of polluted air from outside.
“Those who are unwell are advised to seek immediate treatment at the nearest health facility, while information on measures to reduce the health effects of haze is available on the MOH’s InfoSihat website,” it said.
The MOH also urged the public not to engage in open burning or allow irresponsible parties to trespass on their land or premises for such activities. — Bernama

Title: MACC detains seven in Tabung Haji RCI probe, including senior executives and shipping company CEO
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 15 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has detained seven people as part of its investigation into the findings of the RCI report on Tabung Haji (TH).
According to sources, the suspects, comprising a chief executive officer, a former director, a director and four former TH senior executives, were arrested separately between 3pm and 10.30pm last night at the MACC headquarters in Putrajaya.
“The first suspect, a shipping company CEO with a ‘Datuk’ title in his 60s, was arrested on suspicion of submitting documents with false details when making payments to TH. It involved falsifying a petroleum company contract to benefit his own firm.
“The second suspect is a construction company director with a ‘Datuk’ title, also in his 60s. He is suspected of deceiving TH officers into investing in a construction company with a promise that the firm had potential to be listed on Bursa Malaysia,” the source said.
The third suspect, a former company director with a ‘Datuk Seri’ title in his 60s, was arrested on suspicion of being involved in the same matter as the second suspect, the source added.
Meanwhile, four former senior TH management members, aged between 50 and 60, including one with a “Datuk Seri” title and a woman, were arrested on suspicion of being involved in corrupt practices leading TH into a hotel lease with a company in Saudi Arabia worth SR2.49 billion, resulting in losses to the pilgrimage fund.
Sources said only the shipping company CEO and construction company director were remanded, while the other five suspects were released on MACC bail for health reasons.
Magistrate Ahmad Afiq Hasan issued a five-day remand order until August 19 for both suspects after allowing MACC’s application at the Putrajaya Magistrates’ Court this morning.
MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman confirmed the arrests when contacted, and said the case is being investigated under Sections 18 and 16(a)(A) of the MACC Act 2009. — Bernama
